Francesco Mansi chose the latter when he selected Hotel Miramalfi’s clifftside location in the 1950s; instead of opening his hotel in the pretty seaside village, he opted for a property with postcard-like vistas of Amalfi and the Tyrrhenian Sea. The hotel’s design makes the most of its position — dazzling views are available from its terraces, restaurant, saltwater pool, guest rooms, and even the parking lot.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: COMO Alpina Dolomites in Alpe di Siusi/Seiser Alm
ld.description: Not many hotels can claim residence within a UNESCO world heritage site, but the spectacular Alpe di Siusi qualify, and the COMO Alpina Dolomites is both immersed in, and inspired by, Italy’s famous peaks. This luxurious lodge offers as adventurous an outdoor experience as you like, paired with all the five-star comforts you can handle, including an elaborate spa. Rooms and suites are spacious and tasteful, Alpine in inspiration though contemporary in style, and each room has a balcony or a terrace with a view. The Lodge’s three restaurants offer both Mediterranean and international fare, with a focus on ecologically sourced ingredients, and the bar and cigar lounge each provide a welcoming space to end — or begin — an evening.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Aman Rosa Alpina in San Cassiano
ld.description: After decades at the very forefront of luxury hospitality, the Aman brand has begun to step out of its comfort zone. First from strictly rural modern-luxe resort enclaves to similarly exquisite urban luxury hotels; lately, with some sensitive yet thorough renovations of historical properties. Aman Rosa Alpina, for example, is an update of a 1930s mountain lodge that was already one of the Dolomites’ best-loved independent hotels. And after a transitional period as an Aman partner hotel, it’s been redesigned and refurbished, and enters the pantheon as a fully fledged Aman resort.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: La Fiermontina Palazzo Bozzi Corso in Lecce
ld.description: The Baroque city of Lecce, on the outer reaches of the Salentine Peninsula, is one of the most picturesque places in Puglia, and perhaps all of southern Italy. It’s here, in a city-center palazzo that dates back to 1775, that siblings Antonia and Giacomo-Fouad Filali established a luxury boutique hotel that showcases not just Lecce’s architectural history but the family’s extensive art-world connections as well. La Fiermontina Palazzo Bozzi Corso is named for the Fiermonte branch of the family; one of its ten suites is named for Lady Astor, to whom Enzo Fiermonte was married.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Casa Cipriani Milano in Milan
ld.description: After the flagship in Manhattan the second Casa Cipriani, the lavish luxury boutique hotel offering by the legendary hospitality concern, finds itself in Milan, in a stately stone edifice next to the Giardini Indro Montanelli, just outside the Quadrilatero d’Oro. Its interiors are the work of none other than Michele Bönan, the Florentine luxury master; its rooms and suites are composed of classic retro elements but feel timelessly contemporary. Like its New York relation it’s also a members’ club, which means you’ll share the spa and the Club Restaurant and Living Room with a who’s-who of stylish locals.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palazzo Petrvs in Orvieto
ld.description: Long abandoned and once home to Renaissance notary Petrvs Facienus, this 16th-century palazzo in the heart of Orvieto has been brought back to life with meticulous effort. Behind its carved stone doorways lie frescoes uncovered beneath centuries of plaster, coffered ceilings restored by hand, and striped textiles. Each of the nine rooms balances restraint with richness; even the restaurant, set in a deconsecrated church, feels conservatively theatrical. Centuries of history, holding their ground in the shadow of the Duomo.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Casa Newton in Pienza
ld.description: On first look, Casa Newton looks like a textbook Tuscan fantasy. And while this countryside estate-turned-boutique hotel has all the trappings — set amid the rolling green landscapes of the Val d’Orcia and enclosed by old stone walls, the property is dotted with olive groves, fragrant herb gardens, and scenic vineyards — it’s a stylish upgrade from the standard agriturismo.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: La Palma Capri, an Oetker Collection Hotel

ld.name: La Palma Capri, an Oetker Collection Hotel in Capri
ld.description: Tipping its hat to the Capri of the 1950s, this landmark hotel sits just a short promenade away from the famous Piazzetta, the heart of fashionable island life. Built in 1822, the hotel’s most recent renovation ensured its continual appeal to international travelers used to high standards of service and comfort. Along with sleek and uncluttered bedrooms and the elegant swimming pool is the very stylish all-day rooftop terrace.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Collegio alla Querce, Auberge Collection in Florence
ld.description: Auberge Resorts chose a slightly out-of-the-way setting for its first hotel in Italy: instead of a location in the historic center of Florence, Collegio alla Querce, Auberge Collection is situated in a prestigious former college founded in 1868 by the Barnabite Fathers on a secluded hilltop overlooking the city. Extensive restorations preserved many of the property’s best features, including original frescoes and coffered wood ceilings, but the local design firm ArchFlorence turned the former classrooms into spacious suites with luxurious stone-lined bathrooms and private wine cellars. The onetime headmaster’s office now serves as a stylish cocktail and cigar lounge, and the olive- and oak-shaded gardens are home to an outdoor pool, the open-air Café Focolare, and the peaceful Aelia spa.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Grand Hotel Majestic  in Bologna
ld.description: Set in an 18th-century palazzo in Bologna’s historic center, the Grand Hotel Majestic già Baglioni is the grand dame of the city's hotel scene. It’s the oldest in town, with a storied past on proud display — remains of an ancient Roman road are visible in the cellar, intricately painted frescoes depicting European history adorn the restaurant’s curved ceilings, and an elegant red-carpeted staircase connects four levels lined in white marble. It’s a landmark that symbolizes old-world grandeur: apart from the updates you’d expect at any luxury hotel, no one’s experimenting with tradition here.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa Corallo in Sant'Omero
ld.description: Not far from the Adriatic coast, near the border of Marche and Abruzzo, Relais Villa Corallo is an elegant getaway in a relatively undiscovered section of central Italy. The stately stone mansion was built as a private residence in the mid-19th century, and much of its old-world character remains. The interiors feature original parquet flooring and ornate fireplaces, grand staircases and glittering chandeliers, while the surrounding park, shaded by oak and cypress trees, is laced with paths to explore on foot or bicycle. Suites are all unique, with details like four-poster beds, designer wallpaper, and light-filled marble bathrooms with freestanding tubs. The estate’s organic farm sources most of the ingredients for the hotel’s refined Retrovilla Bistrot — even the olive oil is pressed on site, using olives from the trees by the pool.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Interno Marche in Tolentino
ld.description: In the Marche town of Tolentino, Interno Marche has taken a historic building and given each of its 30 rooms to a different design icon: minimalist, radical, futurist, pop, so that the hotel functions more like a design tour than a conventional stay. Frescoed ceilings in some rooms play against sharp contemporary furnishings; others go deep into bold color and mid-century references. The restaurant, L’Opificio, works through the flavors of the Marche region, and a spa with an indoor pool rounds out what is, for this part of central Italy, an unusually ambitious property.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Berghoferin Fine Hotel & Hideaway in Redagno
ld.description: Built in the 1960s and adapted in 2022, this 13-suite hideaway in the South Tyrolean hills takes a maximum of 26 guests at a time, a deliberate ceiling that shapes everything about the experience. Swiss pine, Farrow & Ball in dozens of shades, Joseph Frank textiles sourced from Svenskt Tenn in Stockholm, and 15th-century paneling in the stübli give each room its own character. The spa was carved from the old basement garage. Dinner rotates nightly between the smoking room, the book-lined snug, and the stübli. Alto Adige wines are poured with real knowledge and care.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Baglio Oneto in Marsala
ld.description: Once a fortified residence home to one of Italy’s noblest families, and still owned by its descendants today, Baglio Oneto celebrates the region’s long tradition of Marsala wine making, although staying here isn’t limited to just oenophiles. The hotel’s picturesque spot on the coast of western Sicily, surrounded by 35,000 square meters of vineyards, ancient olive trees, and various flora and fauna, suits anyone looking to slow down and switch off. As do the facilities, which include a saltwater infinity pool with a view across the Stagnone Nature Reserve and Egadi Islands.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Torre Fiore Hotel Masseria in Pisticci
ld.description: Italy’s farmhouse hotels come in a multitude of shapes and sizes, differing region by region; if you want to see how Basilicata differs from Tuscany or Umbria, compare Torre Fiore Hotel Masseria with its more typical northern cousins. This whitewashed structure is uniquely ornamented, and is surrounded, village-like, by the hotel’s 13 rooms and suites. Its hilltop perch offers a view of the not-so-distant Ionian Sea, and its small size ensures that the hospitality feels personal.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bra Hotel in Bari
ld.description: The Puglian city of Bari is newly resurgent, and its hospitality scene is evolving to match. Bra Hotel is set in Murat, the center of modern Bari, yet it’s barely three streets away from either the waterfront or the historic Bari Vecchia. Inside, it’s the kind of urbanely stylish and tastefully luxurious hotel that was largely absent this side of Rome.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Wine Relais Feudi del Pisciotto in Niscemi
ld.description: Set among sun-bleached vineyards in Sicily’s remote southeast, Wine Relais Feudi del Pisciotto is an 18th-century estate turned boutique wine hotel with a deep connection to its landscape, and a cellar to match. The setting is wonderfully isolated, save for the agricultural town of Niscemi ten minutes away. Rooms are spread across former farm buildings, some with original features like stone troughs or panoramic terraces, while others occupy the recently restored aristocratic residence. There’s a generous pool, a small spa, and pine-shaded paths that open onto wide views of the surrounding hills.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed on request (charges apply).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: ADLER Sicilia in Siculiana
ld.description: ADLER Sicilia is set on a protected stretch of coastline within the Torre Salsa nature reserve, where Mediterranean views and eco-conscious design go hand in hand. Built with local clay, volcanic stone, and cedar wood, the resort sits low on the land, designed to follow the contours of its setting. Suites are minimalist and low-slung, each with a private terrace facing the sea or gardens. The spa is expansive, with panoramic saunas, thalasso pools, and sea-view treatment rooms. Days here can be as active or unhurried as you like, with coastal hikes, fitness classes, and delicious Sicilian cooking drawn from the estate itself.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Villa Sant'Andrea, A Belmond Hotel in Taormina
ld.description: An enchanting seaside villa, built in 1919 by the Cornish Trewhella family, now hosts this stunning property, a true embodiment of Sicilian-style Dolce Vita. In the common areas — lobby, bar, and restaurant — shades of green and blue set the mood, while the walls come alive with vibrant works by local artist Alessandro Florio, inspired by the colors of traditional Sicilian carts.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Le Sirenuse in Positano
ld.description: Seldom has there been a name more poetic or appropriate. Rising out in the dreamy, sun drenched seaside town of Positano, covered with climbing grape trellises, the appellation for this eighteenth century summer house is simply Italian for “the sirens.”

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Castiglion del Bosco, A Rosewood Hotel

ld.name: Castiglion del Bosco, A Rosewood Hotel in Montalcino
ld.description: This place is a big deal. There aren’t a lot of rooms, but in every other way it’s a big deal none the less. Basically, the intimate hotel portion of Rosewood Castiglion del Bosco is just the tip of the bucolic iceberg — in total, more than 5,000 acres of intact, 900-year-old agricultural estate property provide a spectacular backdrop. Wine is actively produced here and much of the property is comprised of preserved lands for grape growing or forests. The rest has been sensitively formed into a community of sandstone villas, with the original estate buildings at its heart. The idea is for guests to immerse themselves in the landscape, functions and pace of Tuscany, wander the massive property as if it’s the year 1552 and the estate belongs only to them. But in terms of Tuscan hotel luxury, it's also very much in the here and now, with two restaurants — one of them MICHELIN-Starred — as well as an organic kitchen garden, a cooking school, a fine spa and plentiful sport and fitness facilities.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Jumeirah Capri Palace in Capri
ld.description: It’s in the center of Anacapri, on the quieter side of this spectacular island, that you’ll find Capri Palace Jumeirah, a longtime favorite among in-the-know Capri travelers; the location, right next to the chairlift that ascends Mount Solaro, is as prominent as can be, yet it remains untroubled by the crowds that gather further east.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Hotel Principe di Savoia, Dorchester Collection

ld.name: Hotel Principe di Savoia, Dorchester Collection in Milan
ld.description: The Principe is a classic — the Milanese hotel against which all other Milanese hotels are measured. Though the amenities are modern, there’s a sense in which the atmosphere of the place has stayed the same for the last hundred years — crystal chandeliers, intricately carved antique furniture, elegant carpets and moquette, refined upholstery, sumptuous velvets, and opulent draperies.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bvlgari Hotel Milano in Milan
ld.description: It’s not the most prominent hotel in the city, but its location is one of Bvlgari Hotel Milano’s great strengths. It’s set on an acre of gardens, at the end of a private street between the Quadrilatero della Moda and the Brera — discreetly sequestered, but close by to the heart of Milan. Its design, by Antonio Citterio & Partners, is the last word in contemporary Italian luxury. And the experience is an unforgettable one, worthy of being the first hotel to bear the Bvlgari name.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Il Pellicano in Porto Ercole
ld.description: In a way, Il Pellicano's location is notable for its lack of competing attractions. Many of Italy’s most extraordinary hotels are set in places that are elbow-to-elbow with hotels, and just as packed with travelers. Not so here. This region of southern Tuscany, the Maremma, was undiscovered country for international travelers when Il Pellicano opened its doors in the Sixties. And even today, under the ownership of the same family’s next generation, Il Pellicano is a destination unto itself.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: San Domenico Palace, Taormina, A Four Seasons Hotel

ld.name: San Domenico Palace, Taormina, A Four Seasons Hotel in Taormina
ld.description: The Sicilian town of Taormina is nothing if not spectacular, with the Ionian Sea at its feet and Mount Etna at its back. No less spectacular is San Domenico Palace, Taormina, A Four Seasons Hotel — first a 14th-century convent, later a 19th-century grand hotel, playing host to everyone from Oscar Wilde to Audrey Hepburn. And now, as a member of the Four Seasons family, it’s simply a top-flight luxury resort, made newly famous as the setting for the second season of The White Lotus.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Dogs under 22 lbs / 10kg are allowed, except in suites with plunge pools or jet tubs, where pets are not permitted. Limit of one pet per reservation. Additional nightly charges apply.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

pages.h1: Castello di Casole, A Belmond Hotel, Tuscany

ld.name: Castello di Casole, A Belmond Hotel, Tuscany in Casole d'Elsa
ld.description: This sort of thing is why the word Tuscany carries such rich connotations all around the world. Hotel Castello di Casole stands on the site of a thousand-year-old aristocratic estate, the fruit of years of meticulous restoration by an American ownership team and an army of Italian architects and designers. It’s a restoration that was rigorously historical where it could afford to be, and yet wasn’t afraid to take some very welcome liberties — the atmosphere is timeless, classic Italian country living, which is only enhanced by the addition of modern marble baths and up-to-date electronic amenities.
ld.petsAllowed: We allow only small pets 10kg and under. They are welcome free of charge. Pets are not permitted in the restaurants- fitness center- spa or pool area.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Firenze in Florence
ld.description: One of the most common complaints about the big luxury chains is that they tend to exhibit a certain sameness of style, no matter the location. But whatever you might say about the Four Seasons Firenze, you certainly can’t get away with saying that. Never mind the museums and the galleries — you could give yourself an attack of Stendhal syndrome without even leaving the hotel, especially if you walk in expecting a more typically beige sort of luxury.
ld.petsAllowed: \n One pet 30kg or under is allowed per room. Additional charges apply.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

pages.h1: Hotel Cipriani, A Belmond Hotel, Venice

ld.name: Hotel Cipriani, A Belmond Hotel, Venice in Venice
ld.description: Venice’s most famous hotel is neither a landmark palace, nor several hundred years old, and it stands not in the city proper, but across the lagoon on Giudecca Island. Nonetheless, the Hotel Cipriani is as synonymous with Venice as the Piazza San Marco. We suppose it has to do with the founder Giuseppe Cipriani, whose 1931 Harry’s Bar sated Hemingway’s legendary thirst, as well the only slightly less legendary thirsts of F. Scott Fitzgerald, Noël Coward and Gertrude Stein.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Vigilius Mountain Resort in Lana
ld.description: Vigilius Mountain Resort is set on Mount San Vigilio, at an altitude of 1,500 metres, and is accessible only by cable car. The design of the resort itself is strikingly modern — blonde on blonde, lots of bare wood and exposed timbers, and a healthy dose of stone and concrete, blunting any tendencies toward log cabin-ness.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Grand Hotel Timeo, A Belmond Hotel, Taormina

ld.name: Grand Hotel Timeo, A Belmond Hotel, Taormina in Taormina
ld.description: Nestled beside the Greek Theatre and offering a unique view of the sea and Mount Etna, the Belmond Grand Hotel Timeo has stood as an opulent symbol of Sicilian aristocracy since 1873. It has welcomed guests such as Oscar Wilde, D. H. Lawrence, Guy de Maupassant, and Kaiser Wilhelm II — all undoubtedly captivated by the sublime views and the grandeur of the Timeo’s interiors, adorned with Sicilian Baroque flourishes.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Eden, Dorchester Collection in Rome
ld.description: Rome’s Hotel Eden was already worthy of the name — it’s been among the leading lights of Roman luxury hospitality since its opening at the end of the 19th century. Today it’s a member of the Dorchester Collection, a name that’s familiar indeed to patrons of high-fashion luxury hotels.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: EALA My Lakeside Dream in Limone sul Garda
ld.description: To go along with its unusual name, derived from the Celtic word for “swan,” EALA My Lakeside Dream styles itself an “adult-friendly” hotel — meaning this luxury hotel, on the shores of Lake Garda, is meant to convey a tranquil, private, and romantic atmosphere. Its terraced construction gives its suites plentiful private balcony space, and its minimalist, modernist-inspired interiors are nothing if not refined. Glass-walled bathrooms and/or in-room soaking tubs increase the intimacy, and the spa is a refuge for body and mind. Restaurants include the fine-dining Senso Lake Garda Alfio Ghezzi and the less formal Alfio Ghezzi Bistrot.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Casa Maria Luigia in Modena
ld.description: You can bet that a country-house hotel by an award-winning chef of Massimo Bottura’s caliber would be a compelling culinary destination; less self-evident is that it would be so impressive a lodging in its own right. Casa Maria Luigia is intimate, but it’s far from sleepy, thanks to lively boutique-style interior design and a quality collection of modern furniture and contemporary art. You’re 15 minutes’ drive from Modena, but many guests are content to remain on site, exploring the estate’s gardens and grounds, which include a swimming pool, a tennis court, and a fitness center that does double duty as an art gallery.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Milano in Milan
ld.description: The Four Seasons Hotel Milano is located in an exceptional place: in the heart of the Fashion District, a 15th-century monastery arranged around a tree-lined cloister is the dream location you wouldn't expect to find in the heart of the city. Among all the luxury hotels in Milan, this one is certainly the most steeped in history, as evidenced by the fragments of Renaissance frescoes, the ogival vaults, and the ancient fireplaces that harmoniously coexist with modern and sophisticated furnishings, further refreshed by the renovation of the common areas by Patricia Urquiola in 2021. In 2025, it was the turn of the rooms, reinterpreted in a refined and cosmopolitan style by Pierre-Yves Rochon.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets under 25 lbs are allowed in all room categories. Pets must be fully trained, vaccinated, always appropriately restrained and compliant with local legislation requirements.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Milan in Milan
ld.description: Milan is hardly uncharted territory for luxury brands. The world’s high-end hoteliers, in particular, are at the top of their game here, going out of their way to adapt their five-star offerings to the particular style and character of the city — to its 18th-century architecture as well as its status as a capital of contemporary design. Add Mandarin Oriental to this rarefied list. Spanning four classic buildings around the corner from La Scala, the Mandarin Oriental Milan went straight to the source: architect and designer Antonio Citterio, the man who’s responsible for far more than his fair share of Italy’s contemporary luxury interiors.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Borgo Santandrea in Amalfi
ld.description: It takes a fine hotel to stand out amid the legends of the Amalfi Coast, but the ultra-chic, ultra-luxe Borgo Santandrea seems up to the task. It’s a Sixties modernist structure, thoroughly renovated under the direction of architect Rino Gambardella, and it’s full of classic mid-century furniture from the owner’s private collection, all reupholstered in Italian-made fabrics. Virtually everything else is new, from the tile floors to the landscaping, but it all feels perfectly at home, as though it’s always been here; Alici, the terrace restaurant, takes in a commanding view of the spectacular coastline.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Palazzo Portinari Salviati Residenza D'Epoca in Florence
ld.description: The name more or less says it all; Palazzo Portinari Salviati Residenza d’Epoca occupies the famous 15th-century palazzo that was once home to no less luminous a figure than Dante’s Beatrice, and aims to recreate the romance of the era for a modern audience. It helps that it’s practically right around the corner from Florence’s iconic medieval cathedral, and that its 13 suites contain all the luxuries of a contemporary Italian luxury hotel, in spite of their Renaissance-era aesthetics. Other inducements include the luxe Vita Nova spa and the MICHELIN-Starred restaurant Atto di Vito Mollica.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Laqua by the Lake in Pettenasco
ld.description: Though less famous than Lake Maggiore and Lake Como, Lake Orta is scarcely less spectacular; and without quite so long a history of opulent grand hotels to deal with, a place like Laqua by the Lake is free to express itself in an unapologetically modernist direction. No mere rooms, all 18 units are somewhere in the space between suites and apartments; those with views of the lake are worth the premium. There’s a small spa with a CryoSuite as well as an infinity pool and a beach club, and the restaurant and bar serve modern Mediterranea fare under the direction of the award-winning chef Antonino Cannavacciuolo.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Ca’ di Dio in Venice
ld.description: The greatest luxury a Venetian hotel can provide is a proper refuge from the perennially busy street life, and Ca’ di Dio, set in the Arsenale district where the Biennale takes place, does just that. It’s a classic house overlooking the lagoon, a patchwork that dates back many centuries, but it’s been thoroughly updated to modern luxury-hotel standards with an emphasis on high-end contemporary Italian design — and, as ever, it surrounds a trio of blissfully tranquil courtyards. The design is stylish and unique, the atmosphere is hip yet historically aware, and the restaurants serve a remarkably authentic take on the Venetian culinary traditions.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palazzo Venart Luxury Hotel in Venice
ld.description: Venice does luxury hotels its own way; here a 16th-century palace divided into a mere 18 rooms is typical of the genre. Palazzo Venart Luxury Hotel is atypical in a few ways, however — it’s uncommonly secluded and quiet, for one thing, though it’s mere yards from the Grand Canal. The rooms are precisely as ornate and opulent as you’d want a 16th-century palazzo to be; you don’t need a view of the canals to know without a doubt you’re in Venice. And the cuisine is also far beyond typical: GLAM, under the direction of chefs Enrico Bartolini and Donato Ascani, has earned a pair of MICHELIN Stars.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The St. Regis Florence in Florence
ld.description: A stylish Florentine palazzo originally planned by Brunelleschi, with tastefully furnished and elegant interiors. The decor in the guestrooms – some with views of the Arno – reinterprets traditional Tuscan style with ceilings evoking the Medici and Renaissance periods in the more interesting rooms, while the fabrics and colours are typically local in style.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bvlgari Hotel Roma in Rome
ld.description: Nearly two decades after the Bulgari Hotel Milan, in 2023 the Roman luxury jeweler has come home, to a monumental 1930s building on the Piazza Augusto Imperatore. Like the other Bulgari hotels its architecture and interiors are the work of modern masters Antonio Citterio and Patricia Viel, who have breathed new life into the building, using the best of Italian craftsmanship and artisans to create environments of refined, composed elegance. Like anything Bulgari touches the experience is thoroughly high-end. The spa, with its jaw-dropping Bisazza mosaic tile pool, is nothing short of spectacular, while the equally impressive Il Ristorante – Niko Romito is joined by a handful of bars and lounges arranged on panoramic terraces decorated by 200 native plants.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

pages.h1: Hotel de Russie, a Rocco Forte Hotel

ld.name: Hotel de Russie, a Rocco Forte Hotel in Rome
ld.description: Built in 1818, the hotel is distinguished by its discreet façade, which conceals a magnificent 0.7-acre garden designed by Giuseppe Valadier — a lush oasis of palm trees, citrus plants, climbing roses, and glimpses of ancient ruins. In the distance, the view of the Pincio and Villa Borghese completes a cinematic tableau that makes every stay truly unforgettable.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Villa Cortine in Sirmione
ld.description: It’s staggering when you stop to think just how many iconic destinations Italy contains. The lake district of the north would be the absolute pride in a lesser country; here it’s one among many unmissable attractions. All of which is the long way around to saying that Lake Garda is something special indeed. By extension, a hotel created from an aristocratic residence surrounded by acres of gardens and parkland with a view of the lake — a hotel like, say, Palace Hotel Villa Cortine — would be nothing short of extraordinary.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mezzatorre Hotel & Thermal Spa in Island of Ischia
ld.description: Just 18 miles from the clamorous, chaotic seaport of Naples, and just a ferry ride from Capri, is the alarmingly beautiful island of Ischia — perhaps the perfect reminder of what has drawn tourists to this part of the world since time immemorial. How do you improve on Italy’s renowned landscapes and hospitality traditions? You concentrate them via island living. Given the readily available volcanic soil and geothermic treatments here, a wellness retreat like Mezzatorre Hotel & Thermal Spa should satisfy even the most frazzled of travelers.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Grand Hotel Miramare in Santa Margherita Ligure
ld.description: In Santa Margherita Ligure, one of the most charming seaside towns of the Riviera, the Grand Hotel Miramare rises proudly above the waterfront — a magnificent palace with the timeless charm of a grand Art Nouveau villa, reminiscent of an ornate wedding cake.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Villa San Michele, A Belmond Hotel, Florence

ld.name: Villa San Michele, A Belmond Hotel, Florence in Fiesole
ld.description: Florence is nothing if not beautiful, but Stendhal syndrome is real — there’s so much to do and to see in its dense city center that even the hardiest travelers risk becoming overwhelmed. It’s for this reason that Villa San Michele, a Belmond Hotel, is so restful — its setting, in the hillside enclave of Fiesole, offers it a measure of seclusion, as well as picturesque views over Florence proper. Well, that and the small matter of the villa itself, whose façade is said to have been designed by no less eminent a hand than that of Michelangelo.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: FORESTIS Dolomites in Brixen
ld.description: Welcome to Forestis Dolomites, a strikingly modern luxury lodge in a densely forested region of South Tyrol. Built of stone, glass, and wood both inside and out, the hotel is beautifully integrated into the landscape. The interior design makes the most of the location; guest rooms are bathed in natural light, thanks to picture windows that open onto views of the wilderness. Each has parquet floors, a king-sized bed, a walk-in shower, and custom bath products; the penthouse suite has a terrace and a private pool with a sauna. An excellent slow-food restaurant provides a nourishing breakfast buffet and peaceful mountain views before skiing, hiking, or cycling. Unwind at the spa, in the garden, or at the bar, with indoor and outdoor fireplaces, and drinks made with herbs and berries foraged from the woods.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Petra Segreta Resort & Spa in Costa Smeralda
ld.description: Let’s say you’re an experienced Italian traveler — visited every vineyard, stayed in every villa, summited every hillside and seen every view, from the canals of Venice to the Roman roads and the coast of Sicily. Just when you’re about to feel jaded (if such a thing is even possible), you remember: there’s still Sardinia. Petra Segreta Resort & Spa combines the best of several worlds in Italian hospitality — equal parts Tuscan villa, rough and rugged southern stonework, and the sort of vaguely volcanic landscape that recalls Sicily or Capri at their most dramatic, accompanied by the white sand beaches for which the Costa Smeralda is justifiably famous.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Caruso, A Belmond Hotel, Amalfi Coast

ld.name: Caruso, A Belmond Hotel, Amalfi Coast in Ravello
ld.description: Any way you look at it, the Caruso is among the finest hotels in Ravello. For some, that’s recommendation enough; for the benefit of the others, though, we’ll go on.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bellevue Syrene 1820 in Sorrento
ld.description: This classic five-star hotel has been an Italian favorite since its opening in 1820, and it’s easy to see why: this cliffside villa looks out over the waterfront and the Bay of Naples from one of Sorrento’s most privileged positions. To this day the Bellevue Syrene drips with 19th-century elegance, scarcely diminished by the recent renovations — while some of the furnishings and décor have been modernized, the atmosphere as a whole is as regal as ever.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Splendido, A Belmond Hotel, Portofino in Portofino
ld.description: Safe to say this one lives up to its name. Splendido, a Belmond Hotel, Portofino is a Ligurian classic, and a longtime favorite among Italian grand hotels — Edward VIII, Duke of Windsor was the first person to sign the guest book in 1901. Today it’s as fine as it ever was, subtly modernized and continually updated, but always true to the historical spirit of the original Splendido.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Caesar Augustus in Capri
ld.description: Enough has been written about the star-studded resorts on the island of Capri to fill a thousand magazines — and still there’s a side to the island that is unfamiliar to the boatloads of tourists ferried in for the day. Anacapri is the hilltop village, towering above the sea, and it’s not only in the literal sense that it is above it all: this is where the crowd-shy traveler checks in, to escape from industrialized tourism.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Masseria Torre Maizza, a Rocco Forte Hotel

ld.name: Masseria Torre Maizza, a Rocco Forte Hotel in Savelletri di Fasano
ld.description: Time was, the notion of living the high life in Puglia was oxymoronic. This is a region that historically was down-at-heel in more ways than simply the geographic one, and even as the hotels started sprouting, they were more likely to be rustic farmhouses than high-gloss boutiques. The Masseria Torre Maizza, then, is a bit of a change of pace: while the main whitewashed farmhouse is a perfect example of the traditional local style, the interiors edge toward the luxurious.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: The Gritti Palace, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Venice

ld.name: The Gritti Palace, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Venice in Venice
ld.description: The word “iconic” has lost some of its impact through repetition, but there’s no better way to describe Venice’s opulent Hotel Gritti Palace. The location could hardly be more auspicious, right on the Grand Canal, across from the Peggy Guggenheim Collection and the distinctive domes of the Basilica di Santa Maria della Salute. And the palazzo itself is certainly not without distinction — it was built in the 15th century, and was the home of the Doge Gritti for whom it’s named.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Villa Igiea, a Rocco Forte Hotel

ld.name: Villa Igiea, a Rocco Forte Hotel in Palermo
ld.description: Designed by architect Ernesto Basile for the Florio family, Villa Igiea, now part of Rocco Forte Hotels, is a stunning Art Nouveau masterpiece. Guests are welcomed into luxurious surroundings, including terraced gardens with sea views, Belle Époque halls, period furnishings, and frescoes.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Milla Montis in Meransen
ld.description: In its broadest contours this South Tyrol hotel is true to Alpine lodge tradition — but its asymmetrical rooflines, its slate-gray larch cladding, and the swooping, organic curves of its façade reveal that Milla Montis is as modern as can be. The interiors follow suit, in acres of warm ash with forest-green woolen furniture — inside and out, it’s all the work of Milanese architect Peter Pichler. Design aside, however, Milla Montis is an absolutely classic Tyrolean lodge, complete with a spa, hearty locally sourced cuisine, and activities that make the most of the Dolomites, in winter and summer alike.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palazzo Parigi Hotel & Grand Spa in Milan
ld.description: Though it’s named for Paris, and its rooms were designed by none other than Pierre-Yves Rochon, this is a hotel that could only happen in Milan. Palazzo Parigi Hotel & Grand Spa is a monument to the sort of opulence that emerges at the intersection of Italy’s fashion and finance industries; its owner, architect Paola Giambelli, has created a unique independent hotel that’s on a level with any of the established luxury players, and as memorable as any boutique.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa Làrio in Pognana Lario
ld.description: It’s Lago di Como to you — and to George Clooney, and Sir Richard Branson, and all the other rich and famous foreigners who own vacation villas here — but for the wealthy aristocrats who retreated to the shores of the glacial lake in Roman times, it was “Lario.” A lavish all-suites hotel, Villa Làrio, takes inspiration from the original Latin name, and from the region’s long history as an elegant getaway for city-dwellers, and anyone else who can afford it.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Castello di Monterone in Perugia
ld.description: Just outside of Perugia, on the “via regalis” or royal road to Assisi, stands a 13th-century castle whose medieval atmosphere makes it a one-of-a-kind luxury boutique hotel. Hotel Castello di Monterone’s 18 rooms and suites add contemporary comfort to old stone walls and well-worn frescoes, and a swimming pool, sauna, and steam room are welcome additions as well. An outdoor terrace looks over the Umbrian countryside from the castle’s hilltop perch, and the hotel’s restaurant opens onto this view; its menu is surprisingly modern, as is the presentation, from the furnishings and artworks to the carefully composed plates.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Hotel de la Ville, a Rocco Forte Hotel

ld.name: Hotel de la Ville, a Rocco Forte Hotel in Rome
ld.description: A brand new Roman grand hotel is rare indeed, but the next best thing is a makeover like the Rocco Forte Hotel de la Ville, which transformed a rather staid luxury hotel by the Spanish Steps into the kind of self-aware fantasy that’s a Forte specialty. It’s on a fine line between tasteful elegance and a slightly over-the-top opulence, without ever feeling kitschy or stuffy. Meanwhile the comforts are first-rate, and the cuisine is a particular delight, featuring a fine-dining restaurant by Fulvio Pierangelini as well as a stunning rooftop terrace and a classic Roman trattoria.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The St. Regis Rome in Rome
ld.description: On January 1894, the Grand Hotel de Rome (renamed St. Regis in 2000) was inaugurated by Cesar Ritz with a grand 16-course dinner for 100 guests, crafted by chef August Escoffier. For over a century (in 2024, the hotel celebrated its 130th anniversary), it has been the preferred address for royal families, diplomatic delegations, and VIPs. As proof of the level of privacy and discretion offered, one wing of the hotel is served by a dedicated elevator and can be completely separated from the rest of the structure.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Cape of Senses in Torri del Benaco
ld.description: The shores of Lake Garda are home to more than a few luxury hotels, but Cape of Senses ascends to new heights. Not just literally, though hillside location places it 800 feet above the lakeshore, but in its scale and ambition — no mere villa, this purpose-built luxury wellness resort comprises 55 rooms, two restaurants, an expansive spa, and an exhaustive array of health-focused activities. The setting is splendidly secluded, and the sense of tranquility is only heighened by the adults-only policy. Some suites come with private infinity-edge pools; every unit looks out over the lake from full-length windows and private terraces.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Baglioni Masseria Muzza in Otranto
ld.description: By now the Puglian farmhouse hotel should be almost as familiar as its Tuscan counterpart; whitewashed stone, arched ceilings, and Baglioni Masseria Muzza is a fine exemplar of the form. It’s set just outside the charming coastal town of Otranto, far down the heel of Italy’s boot, and its 40 rooms and suites are comfortable, expansive, and extraordinarily soothing in their palette of whites, creams, and grays. It’s got a spa whose scale is perhaps surprisingly large, and not only is the beach close by, but the Almini Lakes nature reserve is as well. Return in time to dine on Salentine classics at one of the property's two restaurants.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Passalacqua in Moltrasio
ld.description: Passalacqua, the latest hotel project by the De Santis family – also owners of the Grand Hotel Tremezzo – was designed in the late 18th century for Count Andrea Lucini Passalacqua and quickly became a gathering place for countless prominent figures from the worlds of music, literature, art, and politics. In 1829, Vincenzo Bellini chose it as his residence, composing two of his most famous operas there: Norma and La Sonnambula.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Violino D'Oro in Venice
ld.description: The touristy side of Venice is much commented on, but it’s long forgotten once you’re over the threshold of the Violino d’Oro, a family-owned and -operated boutique hotel mere minutes from the Piazza San Marco. Here the family in question is an impeccably tasteful one, responsible for, among others, Florence’s Grand Hotel Minerva; the atmosphere within the Violino d’Oro is suitably glamorous and eclectic, and feels almost residential in its pervasive sense of calm.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Umiltà 36 in Rome
ld.description: In a location as central as this — practically right around the corner from the Trevi Fountain — a bit of privacy and discretion pays big dividends. Umiltà 36 is tucked away on a side street that connects to the Via del Corso, and behind its door is a luxury boutique hotel whose interiors are alive with a contrast of styles, from Art Deco to classic modernism to modern and contemporary art. The rooms and suites are crisp and clean-lined, no Roman rough edges; public spaces include the Dandy Café restaurant and the brand new seafood restaurant Aquamarina.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Maalot Roma in Rome
ld.description: Young, irreverent and a bit rock 'n' roll… that’s how Maalot likes to define itself. Once you arrive on the lively and bustling Via delle Murate, you can’t miss it: find the Don Pasquale restaurant (named in homage to Donizetti who stayed in the building) and enter this way. The rooms and common areas are arranged around the beautiful hall covered by a glass dome of the restaurant, which becomes a kind of meeting and exchange square. The vibrant and lively atmosphere is reflected in the eclectic, vaguely art deco interiors and furnishings: from the portrait of Marilyn in 18th-century attire in the ground floor lounge to the bold colors of the rooms… here, nothing is whispered! In the spirit of Paul Young’s song ‘Wherever I Lay My Hat (That’s My Home)’, the theme of the hat recurs in various shapes and forms. For a bit of physical activity, the gym awaits in the basement (a luxury in a boutique hotel of the city center). Alternatively, you are just a few steps away from the Trevi Fountain and the Vittoriano.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Romazzino, A Belmond Hotel, Costa Smeralda

ld.name: Romazzino, A Belmond Hotel, Costa Smeralda in Costa Smeralda
ld.description: Romazzino, A Belmond Hotel, Costa Smeralda is, like so much else in Sardinia, both quintessentially Italian and yet distinct from life on the mainland. There’s space here, for one thing, to spread out, and this village-like resort, laid out by the architect Michele Busiri Vici, makes the most of its expansive setting. The rooms, suites and villas are handsome and simple in style, one part rustic and one part modern in inspiration. Gardens line the pathways that lead down to the hotel’s private beach, and the pool and spa are complemented by more active offerings like tennis, hiking, biking and water sports. Restaurant La Terrasse takes it all in from an elevated vantage point, with views over the beach and the bay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palazzo Roma in Rome
ld.description: Rome is full of palaces, but most have been turned into museums or remain private residences, their magnificently frescoed ceilings inaccessible to the public. Palazzo Roma, though — brilliantly restored under the direction of architect Giampiero Panepinto and opened as a luxury hotel in 2023 — offers a rare overnight experience. This 17th-century palace is right on the Via del Corso, a location that couldn't be more convenient for sightseeing and shopping; inside, the interiors evoke the grandeur of the era, the original marble staircase, rich wood paneling, and coffered ceilings all carefully refurbished. The rooms are just as elegant, with modern four-poster beds, original artworks, colorful stripes and patterns, and fresh floral arrangements. Some suites have private terraces.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Airelles Palladio, Venezia in Venice
ld.description: The first Airelles hotel outside of France, Airelles Palladio Venice occupies a splendidly secluded corner of Venice; from this spot on the island of Giudecca, you’re straight across from St. Mark’s Square, but separated by a three-minute boat ride from the passing crowds. The rooms and suites are divided evenly between the Palladio, designed by the Renaissance architect Andrea Palladio, and the elegant Villa Frollo, while the smaller Villa Mason is a private three-bedroom refuge for a family or a larger party.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are welcome (additional charges and conditions may apply).

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Orient Express Venezia in Venice
ld.description: The venerable Orient Express brand still operates a rail experience like no other, and its second hotel property (after La Minerva in Rome) shows another of Europe’s most famous destinations in a rarefied, luxurious light. Orient Express Venezia gives new life to the 15th-century Palazzo Donà Giovannelli, dividing it into 41 rooms and 6 suites that rival any in town — perhaps in all of Europe — in terms of sheer tasteful luxury.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Corinthia Rome in Rome
ld.description: A monumental grand palazzo on the Piazza del Parlamento, in the historic heart of Rome, is an auspicious setting for a 60-room luxury hotel. Corinthia Rome is the product of a substantial renovation that transformed the onetime Bank of Italy into the lavish lodging that it is today. The style is impeccable, even by Roman standards, and the comforts are first-rate; the entry-level rooms are impressive while the suites are nothing short of extravagant. Meanwhile the bank’s old vaults have been transformed into a spa complete with a Roman-style bath, and among the restaurants is the unabashedly high-end Viride by Carlo Cracco.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Carlton, a Rocco Forte Hotel

ld.name: The Carlton, a Rocco Forte Hotel in Milan
ld.description: Milan’s mid-century Carlton is enviably placed in the Quadrilatero della Moda, surrounded by some of the finest high-end retail in the world, and under the guidance of the British-Italian hotelier Rocco Forte it’s reclaimed its status as one of the most desirable lodgings in town. The Carlton, a Rocco Forte hotel combines under one roof everything luxury travelers love about this town, weaving together threads of old-world elegance, modern Italian design, impeccably composed style and a discreet, almost residential atmosphere.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: The James Suite Hotel Firenze 1564 in Florence
ld.description: A 16th-century convent in Sant’Ambrogio, one of Florence's quieter neighborhoods and minutes from the Duomo, The James Suite Hotel has a lot going on inside. Designer James Cavagnani has layered the high-ceilinged rooms with pieces collected from decades of travel: antique furniture, global textiles, unexpected objects, all set against original frescoes and vaulted stonework. Some suites have private patios, others a sauna. The candlelit bar downstairs has a quietly theatrical atmosphere, and the rooftop terrace looks out over the city's terracotta skyline.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Resort Fontes Episcopi in Aragona
ld.description: A former nobleman’s mansion has been transformed into Fontes Episcopi, a rustic resort in the Sicilian countryside. There’s a choice of attractive rooms or private bungalows, which even come with their own courtyards and chaise longues in case you’d like to try sleeping under the stars. The seasonal Sicilian restaurant specializes in pasta homemade with ancient grains, which is one of the dishes that can also be learnt in Fontes Episcopi’s cooking classes. Other activities include olive harvesting, garden therapy, yoga classes, pool time and spa treatments.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Certosa di Maggiano in Siena
ld.description: A 14th-century Carthusian monastery on the outskirts of Siena, Certosa di Maggiano has had an interesting life. In the 1970s it served as the home of artist Anna Ricordati, who hosted Monica Vitti, Alberto Sordi, and other Italian film luminaries within its cloistered walls. Today, the rooms run maximalist: patterned wallpaper, bold tiling, mismatched prints, against the original frescoes and vaulted ceilings. The pool terrace is pink and archway-framed, the Magnolia Bar gathers guests around a fire pit under a centuries-old tree, and Siena's Palio is on the doorstep.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palazzo Boyl 1840 in Cagliari
ld.description: Three cannonballs are still lodged in the façade of Palazzo Boyl, souvenirs of bombardments by the English, Spanish, and French across three separate centuries. The building dates to 1840, raised above Cagliari's port on 13th-century Pisan walls, with the even older Lion Tower absorbed into the structure. The suites take their names from former lives: the Ballroom has soaring timber trusses, the Library keeps its original beams alongside blue Chesterfield sofas, the Kitchens their bare stonework, and On the Roofs delivers exactly what it promises, a terrace suite above the city with water views at sunset.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sunny Valley Mountain Lodge in Santa Caterina Valfurva
ld.description: At 2,700 meters in the Valle dell’Alpe between Santa Caterina Valfurva and Mount Sobretta, Sunny Valley is only visible once the cable car crests the Sobretta ridge, at which point the Stelvio National Park, Europe's largest, opens up in every direction. The lodge is built from local stone and Lapland fir, with 11 individually designed kelo wood suites featuring freestanding bathtubs, artisan furnishings, and floor-to-ceiling windows facing the Ortles-Cevedale peaks. Dining splits across three spaces: wood-fired steaks, a gourmet tasting menu reserved for lodge guests, and a bar with a wine cellar stocked with regional Valtellina labels.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Boutique Hotel Stresa in Stresa
ld.description: An 18th-century lakefront villa in Stresa, left empty for decades before its current owners gave it a full overhaul. Among the town’s more classical properties, this one takes a different approach: mirrored surfaces, brass detailing, velvet chairs in deep greens and blues, with peacock motifs threaded through the decor. All 28 rooms have balconies or terraces, full-height glazing, and complimentary minibars. The rooftop bar looks directly across to Isola Bella and Isola Madre. The restaurant’s chef brings Apulian roots to local lake ingredients, and the gourmet pizzas at lunch are worth making time for.
ld.petsAllowed: \n A maximum of 1 pet is allowed per room.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: La Minerva in Capri
ld.description: A few steps from the Piazzetta and a short walk from Via Tragara, this 19-room family-run hotel descends the hillside on six levels toward its garden pool and the sea beyond. Vaulted ceilings, hand-painted majolica tile floors, sweeping arches, and bougainvillea-draped terraces run through the rooms, most of which face the turquoise Mediterranean. The Emma Premier Room was once the proprietor's private residence; the Laura Junior Suite belonged to the hotel's founder. Breakfast is served on the rooftop terrace each morning, with the 14th-century Charterhouse of San Giacomo and Mount Solaro as the backdrop.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Casa Brera, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Milan

ld.name: Casa Brera, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Milan in Milan
ld.description: Patricia Urquiola rebuilt Pietro Lingeri's 1950s rationalist block into something that honors its severe geometry while softening every interior surface. The lobby's checkerboard marble floors echo the facade's grid, but semi-circular sofas and strategically placed keep the space from feeling rigid. Rooms and suites work with walnut, Fior di Pesco marble, and patterned glass rather than generic luxury finishes. The Brera and Milanese Suites each claim expansive terraces with city views. Dining spans Etereo, the rooftop Italian restaurant beside a heated outdoor pool, Living, an all-day lounge for coffee and cocktails, and Nusr-Et Steakhouse Milano, renowned for its premium grilled meats. The Brera district location puts Teatro alla Scala two minutes away on foot.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Vetera Matera in Matera
ld.description: In a few short years the cave hotels of Matera have evolved from a novelty to one of the hospitality wonders of the world, and the progress continues. Vetera Matera’s opening marked a new high for the “albergo diffuso” genre, its ultra-luxe accommodations ranging from elevated suites with stunning views to subterranean refuges with vaulted ceilings and natural stone walls. Also carved from the porous limestone are the elegant Artema restaurant and the hotel’s elaborate Elysium spa.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Tenuta di Murlo in Perugia
ld.description: Twenty minutes from Perugia, in the impossibly verdant hills of Umbria, is the secluded Murlo Estate, family-owned for centuries and sprawling over thousands of acres. What was once primarily an agricultural concern is now a first-rate luxury resort, the result of a dedicated effort by Alessio and Carlotta Carabba Tettamanti to restore and adapt a wide variety of historical structures, from farmhouses and a water mill to a 14th-century parish church.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Castel Badia in San Lorenzo
ld.description: A Benedictine convent founded in the 11th century, Castel Badia spent two hundred years in ruin before its recent restoration. The original abbesses ruled with unusual autonomy for their time, one even defied the bishopric in the 15th century. Today, twenty-eight rooms occupy the reconstructed fortress, each different in layout and tone, balancing exposed stonework with contemporary furnishings. Seventeen gardens surround the property, including one devoted to medicinal herbs. Fragments of the old chapel and crypt remain open to explore. Five minutes from Plan de Corones, the castle overlooks San Lorenzo di Sebato and the valley below.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Castel Maurn in San Lorenzo
ld.description: In South Tyrol’s Val Pusteria, Castel Maurn turns a centuries-old palace into an eight-suite retreat where frescoed ceilings, vaulted halls, and 18th-century floors meet clean modern lines. Each suite feels residential, with a kitchen, king bed, and generous living space; some add freestanding tubs under painted ceilings. Breakfast arrives in-room, dinners can be privately cooked, and a garden pool and spa invite long pauses after mountain hikes or ski runs on nearby Kronplatz. Under Walter and Sabine’s care, the house has the rare ease of a place that knows exactly what it is.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Ansitz Heufler by Norbert Niederkofler  in Rasen-Antholz
ld.description: In a 16th-century manor once owned by the Hohenbühel zu Heufler family, Norbert Niederkofler has created a retreat that carries his Cook the Mountain philosophy from kitchen to countryside. The Renaissance architecture remains intact: arched stone corridors, carved doors, and the pine-scented Herrenstube with its green tiled stove, yet nine rooms and suites update the story with warm woods, marble baths, and wide mountain views. Set in the quiet Anterselva Valley, it offers the warmth of a family home with the simplicity and clarity of a chef who knows when to let nature lead.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Ancora Cortina in Cortina d'Ampezzo
ld.description: Ancora Cortina is an 1826 original on Corso Italia, its sky-blue shutters open to interiors reshaped by Vicky Charles with owner Renzo Rosso. Thirty-eight rooms and suites include the top-floor Ancora Suite, complete with a broad terrace facing the Dolomites. Expect dark woods, custom pieces, sheepskin and stone fireplaces, plus galleries of vintage Cortina photography and stacks of art books. A Viennese-style terrace dining room serves alpine comfort dishes; there’s a multi-level spa, a gym, and the phone-free Brave Club for cocktails and a suitable soundtrack. Made with a mix of heritage and intention, Ancora feels less like a revival than a return to form: Cortina’s old soul, seen through a sharper lens.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa Treville in Positano
ld.description: Villa Treville isn’t a hotel so much as Positano’s most storied stage set. Once Franco Zeffirelli’s summer residence, it still bears the director’s touch: art, curios, even fragments of opera sets, layered across four villas that tumble down to the sea. The gardens are threaded with secret terraces, pools, and pathways, the kind of spaces where Maria Callas or Leonard Bernstein once escaped the crowds below. Today, only 16 suites preserve the atmosphere of a private residence, each with its own character and outlook on the coast. The shuttle boat service connects the hotel to Positano in less than 10 minutes.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: VISTA Ostuni in Ostuni
ld.description: Between Ostuni’s whitewashed hilltop streets and the Adriatic, Vista Ostuni draws on Puglia’s contrasts: heavy stone walls set against airy vaulted ceilings, shaded interiors giving way to sunlit gardens, the sea on one side and endless olive groves on the other. The hotel’s 28 rooms and suites highlight local craft through stone, wood, and hand-worked textiles, each space carrying its own character. The spa flows into the gardens with two pools, while two restaurants celebrate the seasonality and generosity of southern Italy.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Lake Como EDITION in Griante Cadenabbia
ld.description: On Lake Como’s western shore, with wide views across to Bellagio, The Lake Como EDITION recasts a 19th-century palazzo through a contemporary lens. Interiors combine historic architecture with tailored design: villa-style rooms with king beds, spa-like bathrooms stocked with Le Labo products, and terraces that open directly to the lake. Dining ranges from refined Italian at Renzo to a relaxed poolside setting, while a floating pool, private dock, and curated excursions by boat or on land keep the landscape at the heart of the stay.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: San Luis Retreat Hotel & Lodges in Averlengo
ld.description: San Luis Retreat Hotel & Lodges feels more like a forest clearing than a resort. Tucked into a 40-hectare alpine reserve near Merano, it is built around a still, mirror-like lake and designed to keep you connected to nature with care and intention. Wooden chalets and treehouses, crafted from moon-phase harvested timber, are spaced for privacy, each with oversized windows and natural textures that blur the line between inside and out. The Clubhouse anchors it all, with a restaurant, spa, and a pool that flows toward the lake. It is a place to slow down, where simplicity is deeply felt.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Patria Palace in Lecce
ld.description: Patria Palace faces the sculpted façade of Santa Croce, occupying an 18th-century palazzo that’s been reimagined with Belle Époque flair. The recent revamp introduced deco-inspired furnishings and contemporary art without erasing the building’s original character. Rooms on the piano nobile have tall windows and lofty ceilings, while the top-floor suite comes with a private terrace and jet pool. From this central spot, Lecce’s boutiques and cafés are a short walk away, and in summer, the Adriatic is within easy reach thanks to the hotel’s beach shuttle. Breakfast is served to the sound of a live harp or violin.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Pensione America in Forte dei Marmi
ld.description: Pensione America is the kind of place you might walk past without noticing, until you step through the gate and find yourself in a lush, low-key haven a few blocks from Forte dei Marmi’s beach. Once a humble pensione, it is now an adults-only retreat with just 17 rooms, revived by the Maestrelli family with care and an eye for elegance. Expect breezy coastal interiors, Santa Maria Novella bath products, and a pool framed by lawns and shady verandas. Breakfast is served on the terrace, and guests have first-row access at a nearby beach club. It is a modern take on the long, slow summers Italians do best.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Orient Express La Minerva in Rome
ld.description: After pioneering luxury slow travel since 1883, Orient Express is now encouraging travelers to stop and stay awhile in the Eternal City with the opening of its first ever hotel, La Minerva. The storied property first began life as a 17th century aristocratic mansion before being transformed into one of Rome’s grand hotels in 1811, when it pulled in a creative crowd such as Herman Melville, Stendhal, and George Sand. It has now been restored to its former glory by designer Hugo Toro, who has smoothly blended original elements such as marble statues and ornate Murano chandeliers with a more contemporary Art Deco style. Guests can enjoy evening drinks at La Minerva Bar under the building’s historic skylight, or head to the rooftop restaurant and bar for Mediterranean cuisine and cocktails with a view of the nearby Pantheon and the Roman skyline.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Castell Son Claret in Mallorca
ld.description: The foothills of Mallorca’s spectacular Tramuntana mountain range provide a suitably grand backdrop for Castell Son Claret, a 19th-century castle on an estate that spans more than 300 acres of gardens and untouched parkland. A renovation turned this historic house into a thoroughly luxurious 43-unit boutique hotel, decorated in an understatedly elegant contemporary style.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed, except for therapy dogs when guests are staying in a Pool Suite.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Es Princep in Mallorca
ld.description: Mallorca is known for its picturesque old town, its idyllic seaside, and a warm, organic sort of luxury — but it’s the rare hotel that manages to combine all three. Perched high over the old city walls of Palma de Mallorca, Es Príncep is the exception, a stylish high-end boutique hotel named after the prince who oversaw the construction of the fortifications.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: La Torre del Visco in Teruel
ld.description: Set in the countryside outside the medieval town of Valderrobres, widely considered to be one of Spain’s prettiest villages, the remote Torre del Visco is the only hotel around for miles. The journey is more than worth it, thanks to the efforts of the owners, a madrileño couple who left their publishing jobs three decades ago to restore this semi-ruined 15th-century castle.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Terra Dominicata - Hotel & Winery in Tarragona
ld.description: Two hours due west of Barcelona, in the mountains outside the city of Tarragona, is the spectacular Montsant Natural Park. And in the 12th century, in the foothills to these mountains, a group of Carthusian monks established a monastery and a farm, growing grapes, olives, and other fruits. If they’d been interested in such worldly concerns as real estate, they’d have made a killing, as their taste in locations is unimpeachable — and it’s today’s hotel guests who reap the benefits, as the old monastery, now thoroughly updated, is now open to travelers in the form of Terra Dominicata - Hotel & Winery.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: URSO in Madrid
ld.description: Madrid’s got luxe old grand hotels, and it’s got striking modern boutique hotels. And in Urso Hotel & Spa, it’s got a bit of both. Set in a stately early 20th-century palace, Urso’s neo-classical architecture complements the modernist oak and marble interiors by Antonio Obrador, the celebrated Spanish designer who was also behind its sister hotel Cap Rocat, a majestic, renovated 19th-century military fortress in Majorca. At the center of the city, sandwiched between the residential neighborhood Chamberi and the trendy Chueca district, URSO is surrounded by embassy buildings, local cafés, upscale boutiques, and the new Barceló food market, which delivers the hotel’s fresh Iberico ham daily.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed at URSO Hotel & Spa, and the extra charges for pets will be 49€ per day.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Ramirez de las Casas Deza, 10-12, E-1410

ld.name: Hospes Palacio Del Bailio in Córdoba
ld.description: The Palacio del Baílio is the Córdoba branch of the Hospes franchise, and while the word “Palacio” may put some of us in mind of an old-fashioned grand hotel — like the seaside palaces of Cannes, for example — this is a palace of an entirely different kind. More a mansion than a hotel, it’s equal parts hacienda and Moorish manor, with some rooms opening onto ancillary patios, and others in the main building ringing the main courtyard, with its majestic old palms and pleasantly cool outdoor swimming pool.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pet fee: €40 per stay; only dogs are permitted.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The One Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: There are a lot of great hotels in Barcelona — after all, this is a city that handles a staggering amount of tourism. So why is this the One? Well, for our money, there’s no better location in Barcelona, situated at the point where two of the city’s best neighborhoods meet. There’s Eixample, a leafy residential district south of the Avenguda Diagonal off the beaten tourist path (don’t mistake the Rambla de Catalunya, one of the neighborhood’s charming pedestrian thoroughfares, with its more well-known and highly trafficked counterpart La Rambla). And there’s Gràcia to the north, lively, trendy, and where young Barcelona lives and plays. You’re within walking distance of all the major sights — Gaudí’s Parc Güell, the Sagrada Família cathedral, the Gothic Quarter — but you’re firmly on the locals’ turf. And that makes all the difference.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Carrer del Forn de la Glòria, 14, Palma

ld.name: Can Bordoy Grand House & Garden in Mallorca
ld.description: The old town center of Palma de Mallorca is beautiful, rich with history and impossibly atmospheric. Even so, it’s not quite adequate preparation for what you’ll find within the 12th-century stone walls of Can Bordoy Grand House and Garden. It’s made from a couple of heritage buildings, and the ancient architecture lends its spaces plenty of historical character. But what it all adds up to is a high-end luxury boutique hotel that’s as contemporary as can be.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes, 619-621

ld.name: Almanac Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: A decade or two ago Barcelona’s boutique-hotel style leaned heavily towards dark, moody, eccentric styles, while it was in Madrid that you’d find stately buildings refurbished with contemporary-luxe interiors. Just off the Passeig de Gràcia in the upscale Eixample district, the Almanac Barcelona is an example of the second type: an elegant 19th-century edifice (plus 20th-century addition) whose interiors, by designer Jaime Beriestain, recall several well-loved eras of design history, from Art Deco to mid-century modernism to the present day.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mercer Sevilla in Sevilla
ld.description: If Andalusia feels reminiscent of North Africa, it’s no accident. Sevilla’s got Moorish roots, just like Marrakech. And if a hotel like the Mercer Hotel Sevilla feels a bit like a riad, the inside-out courtyard residences of North Africa, it’s not hard to imagine why. Of course the Andalusian style is unique — there’s a certain ornateness to the architecture along with a simplicity to the décor, and more of a willingness to let that bright sunlight stream in and illuminate these white-on-white spaces. But in the end it’s a remarkably similar concept: an air of sequestered luxury around a beautiful central patio, and a surprisingly small scale, just four rooms and eight suites.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Serras Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: Barcelona is no stranger to impressive boutique hotels, but even against stiff competition, Serras stands out. It’s rare here, or in any city for that matter, to find something that so effortlessly straddles the line between boutique chic and ultra-high-end luxury. It occupies a building of some distinction on the Passeig de Colom, where the Gothic Quarter meets Port Vell, which accounts for one of its most desirable attributes: the marina-facing rooftop pool deck, restaurant, and bar.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Torre del Marqués Hotel Spa & Winery

address.streetAddress: Paraje Torre del Marques, Carretera, a, Km 2,2

ld.name: Torre del Marqués Hotel Spa & Winery in Teruel
ld.description: Between Barcelona and Valencia, set back on the inland side of a small mountain range, is the Aragonese region of Matarraña, home to the beautifully restored 18th-century tower that is the Torre del Marques. Today, after a thorough renovation, it’s an 18-room luxury boutique hotel that offers a farmhouse-style escape, with views of olive groves and vineyards, as well as an environmentally friendly approach and a zero-kilometer cooking philosophy.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Can Cera in Mallorca
ld.description: Strip away the contemporary art and the Egyptian cotton linens, the screens on the walls and the terrycloth robes in the big modern bathrooms, and it’s easy to imagine the original, regal appeal of this traditional Mallorcan mansion. Arriving at Can Cera, passing under its old stone archway and into its leafy central courtyard, you enter a particularly inviting oasis within the already elegant Mediterranean enclave of Palma de Mallorca’s old walled city. A little farther on, up a marble stairway, waits a series of comfy salons, all full of cushiony nooks that invite a respite before continuing to one of the twelve guest rooms. The effect, as you travel from the street to the courtyard to the public spaces to the bedroom, is one of sliding into ever-deeper states of leisure — or, to put it another way, of living like an old-fashioned aristocrat.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: A Quinta da Auga in Santiago de Compostela
ld.description: Situated in a bucolic hectare of countryside just outside the Galician capital city of Santiago de Compostela, A Quinta da Auga is probably the most charming and accommodating paper mill you’ll ever have the pleasure of visiting. That’s former paper mill, of course, one old enough to have acquired a pleasant patina — this 18th-century industrial building has been converted by the Lorenzo Garcia family into a boutique hotel, retaining the original stonework, while the interior has been renovated to provide French-inspired country-manor coziness.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Finca Cortesin in Marbella
ld.description: Southern Spain is blessed with an array of natural gifts: not just sun, sand and surf, but a climate and a landscape that are ideal for the game of golf. And while golf resorts the world over are a conservative lot, Spanish hotels have been quicker than most to modernize — beneath its traditional red tile roofs, the Finca Cortesín is a contemporary-style luxury resort of the new breed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Casa Beatnik Country House in La Coruña
ld.description: It’s clear from the name — and, perhaps, from the vibrant pink of its exterior — that Casa Beatnik Country House isn’t your typical Galician villa-turned-hotel. Here, in Spain’s Rías Baixas wine region, not far from Santiago de Compostela, is a luxury boutique hotel that’s equally dedicated to classic high-end hospitality and chic contemporary fun.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Castillo del Buen Amor in Salamanca
ld.description: Now this is a castle. Not just an aristocratic residence, but a proper fortification, whose heavy stone walls contain a remarkably elegant and comfortable luxury boutique hotel. The castle itself dates back to the eleventh century — that’s a thousand years — and it’s necessarily seen a multitude of different uses during that time. And while it’s been owned by a single family since the Fifties, they’re enthusiastic to share it; the restoration was done largely in the public interest, and there’s no better way to allow modern people to experience it than to let them sleep in it for a night or three.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are only allowed in standard rooms.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Can Mascort Eco Hotel in Costa Brava
ld.description: The notion of a Costa Brava eco-hotel implies a certain beachiness, but Can Mascort Eco Hotel, like many of the finest hotels, avoids the obvious move. About a mile inland from the coast is the medieval town of Palafrugell, and it’s in a restored 17th-century building in the historic center that Can Mascort makes its home.
