In the course of the renovations, the hotel’s proprietors have made this old house a model of sustainability, using only local, natural materials, and making conscious choices to minimize energy use, such as relying, to the greatest extent possible, on natural ventilation and lighting.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Can Alberti 1740 Hotel Boutique in Minorca
ld.description: The historic city of Mahón may be Menorca’s capital, but even at its busiest it’s hardly a bustling metropolis. Even a hotel in the old city center offers more rest and relaxation than stimulating urbanity — a situation that suits Can Alberti 1740 just fine. It’s named for the family that established it as its home and for the year of its foundation, and in its present incarnation as a luxury boutique hotel it trades heavily on its residential atmosphere and its quasi-aristocratic elegance.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Rector in Salamanca
ld.description: Another day, another gorgeous ancient Spanish city, another stunning landmark building turned into a clever, stylish little boutique hotel. Not that we’re complaining. The Hotel Rector in Salamanca is the sort of thing that keeps one coming back again and again. You can only do the major capitals so many times before a certain sameness sets in — a wealth of attractions in secondary and tertiary markets is what makes Spain a perennial destination (see also: Italy).
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Carrer Sant Agustì KM 10.7 , Playa des Arenals 07872

ld.name: Teranka Formentera in Formentera
ld.description: Just south of Ibiza but a world apart, the Spanish island of Formentera is rustic and laid-back, its pristine, pine-forested coastline pleasingly undeveloped. A series of stylish hotels have popped up to accommodate the kind of traveler who’d rather doze on a quiet beach all afternoon than party all night, and Teranka Formentera, set slightly back from Playa Migjorn, is one of the best. The name derives from “terre d’ancrage” — a place to anchor — and that’s just what this boutique resort feels like, a calm haven between the blue sky and the windswept dunes, the interiors mirroring the outdoor landscape while offering protection from the elements.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cap Menorca in Minorca
ld.description: Strategically located in the Mediterranean, Menorca has a rich military history, and in recent years, some of the island’s castles and fortresses have been turned into hotels. Cap Menorca Relais & Chateaux is a rare example of a hotel built on a former military base. High on a cliff over the sea, on a remote, pine-forested stretch of Menorca’s southern coastline, the setting is spectacular — and the hotel’s designers have transformed the place into an idyllic getaway, turning the dusty grounds into tropical gardens and the old military buildings into luxury suites with private saltwater pools.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Brach Madrid - Evok Collection in Madrid
ld.description: Staying anywhere on Madrid’s Gran Vía is a treat, but the new Brach Madrid, a five-star hotel designed by Philippe Starck, offers next-level luxury. The building itself, of course, isn’t new: part of the avenue’s dazzling architectural showcase, it was completed in 1922, initially housing a stylish café-bar on the street level and various designer ateliers on the upper floors. Rich material for Starck’s artistic reimaginings — and he’s made the most of the building’s history, borrowing inspiration from its original style and function to create a hotel that’s glamorous and modern.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cap Rocat in Mallorca
ld.description: What’s so special about Mallorca? The Mediterranean isn’t exactly hurting for islands, and Spain is blessed with stunning landscapes and balmy climes almost from bottom to top. Have a look around Cap Rocat, though, a reconstructed 19th-century fortress set on an 88-acre coastal estate overlooking the Bay of Palma, and you’re quite likely to come away a believer.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: La Residencia, A Belmond Hotel, Mallorca

ld.name: La Residencia, A Belmond Hotel, Mallorca in Mallorca
ld.description: Like most of the world’s fabled tourist destinations, Mallorca has seen its share of development, even verging in places on overdevelopment. This is to one extent or another the natural fate of any desirable locale, yet it need not be all-consuming.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Akelarre in San Sebastian
ld.description: It’s a familiar enough concept in France and even in England, yet for all the distinction of Spain’s high-end restaurant scene, a luxury boutique hotel devoted to a single chef is still something of a novelty here. Just west of Monte Igueldo is where you’ll find Akelarre, a stunning piece of modern architecture which adds 22 luxurious hotel rooms and a full-service spa to Pedro Subijana’s legendary restaurant.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Unico in Madrid
ld.description: By now the idea that Barcelona is the fun one and Madrid is the serious one is simply a long-dead stereotype. But there is something to be said for the way that Madrid’s gems often lie hidden beneath a stately and sober exterior. Hotel Unico is a case in point: behind an elegant 19th-century facade in the city’s swanky Salamanca district is a 44-room boutique hotel that serves up contemporary style with a generous side of sophistication.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: El Llorenç Parc de la Mar

address.streetAddress: Plaça de Llorenç Villalonga, 4, Palma de Mallorca

ld.name: El Llorenç Parc de la Mar in Mallorca
ld.description: Palma de Mallorca is full of extravagantly romantic, old-world-inspired luxury hotels, all of them drawing on both Spanish and Moorish traditions. Not to say there wouldn’t be room for one more excellent one, but El Llorenç Parc de la Mar adds another twist or two to Palma’s rich cultural cocktail. Here designer Magnus Ehrland incorporates modernist furniture and geometric lines, but not in the minimalist way you might have expected half a generation ago — this hotel is warm, eclectic, and full of visual interest.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Can Ferrereta in Mallorca
ld.description: Sister hotel to the impressive Sant Francesc Hotel Singular, in the capital city of Palma, Hotel Can Ferrereta takes to the Mallorcan countryside, to similarly strong results. Like its sister, Can Ferrereta begins with a historical structure — in this case a 17th-century house in the village of Santanyí, near the island’s southeast coast, less than an hour’s drive from Palma.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Sant Francesc Hotel Singular in Mallorca
ld.description: At some point Palma de Mallorca’s best hotels came to rival those in Barcelona and Madrid, two cities that have been in the top league for luxury and boutique hotels from the start. That’s thanks in large part not to the big chains but to one-off independent hotels like Sant Francesc Hotel Singular, a thorough refurbishment of a 19th-century palace that is, in its current incarnation, very much the equal of the long-established names in high-end hospitality.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Torralbenc in Minorca
ld.description: There was a time when, in the travel press at least, the Balearics were known mostly for their youthful exuberance and nonstop party culture. But while nobody was looking, they also set about becoming bastions of tasteful, intimate, small-scale, high-end luxury hospitality. Now they’re the sort of place where Prime Ministers go to unwind. Menorca just might be the last one to embrace this transition — but if Torralbenc is anything to go by, they’re taking to it like old hands.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cristine Bedfor Mahón in Minorca
ld.description: Menorca may be quieter and less visited than some of its Balearic neighbors, but creative small hotels are flourishing on this supposedly “minor” island. Cristine Bedfor, in the Menorcan capital city of Mahón, is a most unusual luxury boutique hotel, in a good way — named for a fictional character dreamt up by hotelier Cristina Lonzano, it’s a multi-layered concept, a local’s vision of a British traveler’s idea of a perfectly hospitable Menorcan residence.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Atrio Restaurante Hotel in Cáceres
ld.description: Even without the hotel, Atrio’s restaurant alone would easily merit a detour. It’s a serious establishment — white tablecloths, finely besuited waiters, diners with similar sartorial inclinations — that’s perfectly matched by a wonderfully peaceful, architecturally striking hotel whose fourteen modern, clean-lined rooms have been masterfully integrated into the stone facade of a much older building in Extremadura’s ancient walled city of Cáceres.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Pepe Vieira in Pontevedra
ld.description: Some restaurant-driven hotels play it safe with their rooms, perhaps unwilling to assume that fans of forward-thinking gastronomy are similarly fans of forward-thinking hospitality. Others, like Galicia’s Pepe Vieira Restaurant & Hotel, wager that as long as they’ve got you thoroughly hooked at the dinner table, you’ll be willing to trust their vision for what the overnight experience should look like.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Monument Hotel in Barcelona
ld.description: Monument Hotel is an elegant five-star hotel that’s opened on the same premises as Restaurante Lasarte, a three-star restaurant by Martín Berasategui, the Basque chef who holds more Michelin stars than any other chef in Spain. Lasarte is a landmark, considered one of the best places to eat in Barcelona, and now it has a hotel to match. Both are located in a grand 19th-century building on the Passeig de Gràcia, a few minutes’ walk from a pair of Antoni Gaudi’s dazzling architectural projects, Casa Battló and La Pedrera. So it seems natural that the Monument Hotel’s striking modern interior, with its curving ceilings and soaring vertical beams, is vaguely reminiscent of Gaudi’s great masterpiece, the Sagrada Familia cathedral.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Convent de La Missió, Grand Luxury Boutique Hotel

ld.name: Convent de La Missió, Grand Luxury Boutique Hotel in Mallorca
ld.description: Tucked down a quiet lane in Palma de Mallorca’s historic quarter is Convent de la Missio, a hotel as modern and stylish as its seventeenth-century exterior is traditional and historic. As the name would suggest, this building was once a convent, and the hotel retains some of the ascetic and sequestered atmosphere appropriate to a convent, providing an oasis of calm amid the bustle of the Old Town (and, in typical Spanish style, some shade from the blinding Mediterranean sun).

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Abadía Retuerta LeDomaine in Valladolid
ld.description: Built from the carefully preserved buildings of a 12th-century abbey, Abadía Retuerta LeDomaine is as historically evocative as any château in France — and, thanks to the work of architect Marco Serra, it’s a first-rate contemporary luxury boutique hotel. It’s set on a vast estate in Valladolid that’s home to some 500 acres of vineyards, a property so large that it can only be properly seen on a guided Jeep tour that ends with a tasting in the old winery’s atmospheric barrel rooms. Other memorable venues for sipping wine include the quaint cloister garden, a courtyard terrace with a telescope for stargazing, and the Calicata Terroir Bar on the vineyard’s edge. The hotel also counts among its attractions the MICHELIN-Starred Refectorio restaurant, the more casual Vinoteca, and a spa that combines wine-country products with the precepts of Tibetan medicine.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed on request. Charges may be applicable.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Hotel Santa María Briones in Briones
ld.description: Northern Spain’s Rioja wine country may be less traveled than the country’s Mediterranean coast, but it’s not a second-class destination by any means. Especially not when it’s got hotels like the Hotel Santa María Briones. Set within the stone walls of a 16th-century manor house, this 16-room luxury boutique hotel makes a compelling case for the Rioja lifestyle: rich history, modern design, artfully prepared local cuisine, and some extraordinary wine.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Wittmore in Barcelona
ld.description: No children are allowed at the Wittmore, and the same goes for photos. Both policies make sense once you step inside this sultry and silent boutique hotel, tucked away on a narrow alleyway in Barcelona’s Gothic Quarter. The hotel leans all the way into the neighborhood's dark, romantic vibes, especially on the ground level with its rich wood paneling, red velvet loveseats, cozy fireplace, and French doors opening onto a courtyard patio. The atmosphere lightens up a bit in the rooms and suites: botanical wallpaper, vintage telephones, and floor-to-ceiling windows opening onto the patio's greenery. Up on the rooftop terrace, the atmosphere is downright cheerful, and it’s especially enchanting at sunset.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cavalta Boutique Hotel in Sevilla
ld.description: Seville has plenty of luxury hotels; until recently, they were all on one side of the river, clustered around the cathedral and the Alcázar. Cavalta Boutique Hotel is the first high-end property on the other side, in the Triana quarter, best known as the birthplace of flamenco. This 12-room boutique hotel, occupying a quaint corner building with wrought-iron balconies and cheerful ceramic tilework, stays true to the neighborhood’s bohemian roots. Rooms are simple and modern, with natural wood flooring, exposed brick walls, and colorful details from decorative headboards to emerald-green accent walls. It’s the common spaces that bring Cavalta to the next level, including a lovely rooftop garden, pool, and cocktail bar. The restaurant, Balbuena y Huertas, restaurant serves as a stylish meeting point for locals and travelers alike.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are welcome in the hotel for a fee of 50€/night, which includes a welcome kit with the following services: pet bed, drinker/feeder, complimentary snack, hygienic bags, water, and a personalized welcome card.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Gran Hotel Mas D'en Bruno in Torroja del Priorat
ld.description: Southwest of Barcelona, Gran Hotel Mas d’en Bruno is nestled on a historic estate in the heart of a majestic landscape — one defined by mountains, medieval villages, and vineyards. This boutique hotel may have an old soul, but it’s thoroughly modern throughout the public and private spaces. Rooms and suites sport a contemporary style while windows frame views of the rolling vineyard. The pool is an ideal spot for whiling away the afternoon, but don’t miss the spa, tucked inside an ancient wine and olive-oil mill. Wine tasting and fine dining are a hallmark of the experience.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mercer Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: Walking the halls of the Mercer Hotel Barcelona is a bit like hanging out in a forward-thinking gallery of modern design, where the exhibits never close and management lets you stay the night — except here, the impeccable modernist furniture and glass partitions are housed in an ancient defense tower. This is Barcelona’s Gothic Quarter, after all, where you’d be hard-pressed to find buildings that don’t reveal some aspect of the district’s Roman origins.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Miramar Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: Score one for historic preservation, as well as one for modern architecture. This Twenties palace sat disused on a Montjuïc hillside for decades, which was a waste, considering its view of the port, and its semi-idyllic city-park location. Now, though, it’s rather exceeded its original potential — after a thorough renovation, including an audacious modern expansion by the architect Oscar Tusquets, the Miramar is now a luxurious and strikingly stylish 75-room hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Es Raco d'Artà in Mallorca
ld.description: Spain’s Balearic islands are home to a special homegrown style of hospitality; here many an old farmhouse has been transformed into a luxe and exceedingly private escape. Even in this context, though, Es Racó d’Artà is something special: in the size of the estate, which comprises not just a farmhouse but nearly two dozen outlying casas and casitas, as well as in the sheer excellence of its design, by the well-known local architect Toni Esteva. More than a hotel, it’s a wellness-oriented retreat, complete with a spa, yoga and meditation instruction, and a location adjoining the Parc Natural de Llevant, for easy access to a Mallorcan-style variation on the Japanese concept of “forest bathing.”

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Antiga Casa Buenavista in Barcelona
ld.description: What began just over a hundred years ago as a family-owned restaurant in Barcelona, in a central location where El Raval meets L’Eixample, is now a stylish and memorable boutique hotel. Antiga Casa Buenavista is still family-owned, but it’s an impressively professional operation — its rooms come with modern necessities like Nespresso machines and smart TVs, as well as luxurious bathrooms stocked with Natura Bissé products.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Alma Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: All that Gaudí architecture has set the bar rather high for Barcelona’s builders, and the Alma Barcelona proves it’s very much up to the challenge. It’s no cathedral, but its interiors, all minimalist subtlety, epitomize the quieter side of Barcelona’s visual style, which is at its best in the largely residential Eixample. It’s the next best thing to keeping your own pied à terre, just off the legendary shoppers’ boulevard Passeig de Gràcia, but without having to look after your own upkeep and service.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: CoolRooms Palacio Villapanés in Sevilla
ld.description: Hospitality is a tough game, but when you start with a building as stunning as this one, it’s a bit like being born on second base. The hoteliers managed to acquire an 18th-century mansion in Seville’s Santa Cruz district, and with a few bold design strokes they’ve turned it into the Palacio de Villapanés, one of the city’s most fashionable boutique hotels.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Cortijo del Marqués in Granada
ld.description: The idea of the country house hotel might not be as familiar in Spain as it is in England or France, but Cortijo del Marqués is proof that there’s nothing preventing them from operating at the highest level. This Andalusian country manor offers an escape that’s practically unique; half an hour outside of Granada, it’s quiet, surrounded by olive groves, full of ancient charm thanks to its beautifully preserved stone architecture.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are allowed upon request - charges apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Finca Serena Mallorca in Mallorca
ld.description: Mallorca is far from a well-kept secret — mass tourism, in fact, is a point of contention among locals on this island idyll. But a place like Finca Serena has nothing at all to do with mass tourism. Here, hidden away on a hundred acres of olive groves, cypress stands, lavender fields, and vineyards, is a contemporary luxury boutique hotel that feels a world away from the busy beach resorts and the debaucherous nightlife of Palma.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Artist Grand Hotel of Art

ld.name: The Artist Grand Hotel of Art in Bilbao
ld.description: The Artist Grand Hotel of Art is just across from Bilbao's Guggenheim Museum, and it's not surprising that some of the excitement and energy from Frank Gehry's design seems to have spilled over into this hotel. The hotel describes itself as "not just a hotel to stay at, but a colourist microcosmos." It may sound a bit hyperbolic, and we admit it may have lost something in the translation from the Spanish, but nevertheless, it does convey a fairly accurate sense of the bold, almost whimsical nature of the design, courtesy of Javier Mariscal and Fernando Salas.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: s/n Av. Bulevar Príncipe Alfonso de Hohenlohe, Von Hohenlohe, S/N

ld.name: Marbella Club Hotel in Marbella
ld.description: Marbella is one of the Costa del Sol’s most storied destinations, and the Marbella Club is the quintessential Marbella resort — established by Prince Alfonso von Hohenlohe in 1954 and playing host to the cream of the European aristocracy, titled and otherwise, ever since. And as the town has grown and developed (apace with the rest of the Mediterranean coast) the Marbella Club has remained delightfully the same.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Lasala Plaza Hotel - Adults Only in San Sebastian
ld.description: There are modern hotels, and there are historic hotels — and there are hotels that can do a bit of both. Fresh off its hundredth birthday, this 1917 building, with its panoramic views of San Sebastián’s extremely picturesque fishing port, has been reinvented. Behind its meticulously restored period façade, the Lasala Plaza Hotel is a luxury boutique hotel in the contemporary 21st-century style: a tightly focused, minimalistic color palette in blues and grays, plus modern furnishings, contemporary artworks, and the plush-but-restrained comforts that today’s travelers have come to expect from travel in the boutique era.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mas de Torrent in Costa Brava
ld.description: Though converted from an 18th-century farmhouse, Mas de Torrent is anything but the simple rustic bed and breakfast you may expect. Behind these honey-colored stone walls is a stunningly smart luxury hotel to rival any in Spain.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets may be accommodated in the Suite Jardin only at the extra cost of 30 EUR per night. Please advise hotel in advance.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Villa Favorita - Adults Only in San Sebastian
ld.description: They call it a “hotel singular,” and it’s fair to say there’s nothing quite like it: a beautifully preserved 19th-century villa, the last of its kind on La Concha Beach in San Sebastian, Spain, meticulously restored and thoroughly renovated and now doing business as a remarkable luxury boutique hotel. La Villa Favorita stands right on the beachfront promenade, giving it a picturesque view of the bay from its many sea-facing windows.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: CoolRooms Palacio de Atocha in Madrid
ld.description: The sumptuous interiors of this luxury hotel in the heart of Madrid reveal its origins as a 19th-century palace-house, from the richly decorated molded walls and ceilings to the bright and spacious rooms and suites. Add the name of its neighborhood and that of its locally headquartered parent company and you’ve got the full title: CoolRooms Palacio de Atocha.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Palacio de los Duques, Gran Meliá

ld.name: Palacio de los Duques, Gran Meliá in Madrid
ld.description: The Spanish royal city of Madrid is well stocked with opulent hotels, but one of the most luxurious is this representative of a homegrown brand: Palacio de los Duques, a Gran Meliá Hotel. Given the name, it may not surprise you to know that this extravagant city-center hotel was once an aristocratic residence, specifically a 19th-century palace belonging to a pair of dukes. And while the renovation required to bring it up to modern five-star standards was a thorough one, enough of the original architecture remains to ensure that the Palacio still feels like a palace, rather than just another luxury hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Peralada Wine Spa & Golf in Girona
ld.description: A name like Hotel Peralada Wine Spa & Golf doesn’t leave much room for elaboration. In fact it’s just what it says it is: a luxury hotel in the Empordà, between Girona and the French border, featuring a working winery and associated vineyards, a luxurious wine-focused spa, and one of the top golf courses on the Costa Brava. And the name leaves out several features, including a casino, a preserved Carmelite convent, and a generous handful of dining and drinking venues.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: 5 Carrer de la Posada de Terra Santa

ld.name: Boutique Hotel Posada Terra Santa in Mallorca
ld.description: We’ve long admired the fact that Spain’s Balearic islands have plenty of refinement to balance their reputation for hedonism, and there might be no more perfect an example than Mallorca’s Boutique Hotel Posada Terra Santa. Set in the ancient streets of Palma, the capital, it’s a bona fide aristocratic manor house, some five hundred years old, transformed by its new owners into a 26-room boutique hotel that’s as elegant as it is contemporary — the sort of place that helps keep a destination like Mallorca inspiring even after decades in the spotlight.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Soho House Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: Hard to believe there was a time when the Soho House concept felt like something so specific to London that it would resist export. Now, with Soho House members’ clubs on multiple continents, it’s clear that the brand is eminently adaptable. Here Soho House trades central London for the Gothic Quarter of Barcelona, in an 18th-century building whose architecture and interiors put an unmistakably Catalan accent on the eclectic, bohemian-inspired house style.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: La Almunia del Valle in Granada
ld.description: This boutique hotel is built on a hill and blends into the surrounding landscape. It has an attractive lounge - library and contemporary guestrooms, two of which are cube - shaped. The homely dining room, illuminated by a skylight, serves market - fresh cuisine with a contemporary touch.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Anantara Villa Padierna Palace Benahavís Marbella Resort

address.streetAddress: Ctra. De Cádiz, Km 166 Urb. Flamingos Golf Club

ld.name: Anantara Villa Padierna Palace Benahavís Marbella Resort in Marbella
ld.description: Think of the Costa del Sol and you quite naturally imagine your hotel will be right front and center on the beach. Anantara Villa Padierna Palace Benahavís Marbella Resort, in contrast, lies some ten minutes inland — and, as it turns out, that makes all the difference. Well, that, and a few stylistic differences. Rather than the whitewashed Andalusian style you might expect, Padierna Palace is a dead ringer for a Tuscan villa. Not only that, but there’s more than a whiff of English country-house style in the hyper-luxe interiors. Safe to say it’s one of a kind — and it’s got the star-studded guestbook to prove it.
ld.petsAllowed: Please note dogs and cats are allowed, max. weight 25kg. Limited availability, please contact the hotel before booking. A charge of 50€ per day will be applied (max. 2 pets per room) between November and May and 90€ per day between June and October. Guide dogs free of charge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Petunia Ibiza, Beaumier Hotel in Ibiza
ld.description: For a view you could do a lot worse than Es Vedrà, the offshore rock formation that’s a dramatic Ibizan icon. It’s visible from the rooftop terrace at Petunia Ibiza, a boutique hotel in a hillside village on the island’s west coast. It’s also visible from many of its 42 rooms and suites — all of which are stylish in an eminently palatable way, bohemian-rustic in inspiration and extremely photogenic in execution. This is the tranquil, restorative side of Ibizan hospitality: not an all-night party, but a sundown cocktail with a view and dinner at La Mesa d’Es Vedrà.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palacio de Luces in Luces
ld.description: The name hints at what you’ll find at the Palacio de Luces, a 16th-century palace surrounded by verdant gardens in northern Spain, between the Sierra del Sueve mountains and the Atlantic coast. The palace itself is gorgeously restored, its exterior meticulously preserved, and its interiors — plus the necessary modern additions — venture into contemporary design while respecting the hotel's noble past.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel L'Avenida in Mallorca
ld.description: Islands and beaches are a classic combination, but sometimes it pays to head for the hills instead. In this case that means the hilltop town of Sóller, half an hour north of Palma de Mallorca, with a view out to sea over the northern coast of the island. It’s here, in an architecturally distinguished century-old townhouse, that L’Avenida makes its home. It’s elegant enough on the outside, but it’s somehow even more impressive inside, where period architectural details and an eclectic variety of furnishings and décor are unified by the keen eye of a skilled contemporary designer.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Fontsanta Thermal Spa & Wellness in Mallorca
ld.description: The Balearic Islands are plentifully endowed with rocky cliffs, pristine beaches, evergreen forests, and rugged mountains, but only a singular occurrence of natural hot springs. They’re located near the southern coast of Mallorca, and Fontsanta Thermal Spa & Wellness is the closest hotel. So close, in fact, that its spa, built around the springs’ mineral-rich thermal waters, is Fontsanta’s main draw and namesake — the name, after all, means “sacred fountain.” But this quietly stylish adults-only retreat has plenty to offer beyond its subterranean springs, like privileged views over the spectacular landscape and a guests-only beach club on Es Trenc, one of the island’s loveliest stretches of shoreline.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Vincci Selección Unuk in Sevilla
ld.description: Most hotels in European capitals are either proudly historic or unabashedly modern. Vincci Selección Unuk GL, just outside Seville’s old town, pulls off the rare feat of being both at once: this boutique hotel comprises two adjoining houses, one proudly traditional and the other unmistakably industrial. Marble staircases and wrought-iron railings evoke the past, but the romantic Andalusian patio has a retractable roof, and guest rooms come with wood-beamed ceilings and parquet floors as well as Nespresso machines and futuristic bathrooms. In a city where it always feels like summertime it’s hard to go wrong with a series of open-air terraces, including one with a saltwater pool, to say nothing of a rooftop with a stylish bar and restaurant, twinkling lights, and 360-degree views over the city.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: La Fonda Heritage in Marbella
ld.description: Occupying a privileged spot on one of the prettiest plazas in Marbella’s Casco Antiguo, La Fonda Heritage Hotel is a stunner inside and out. The hotel is housed in a trio of 16th-century buildings that have served various functions over the years — church, school, private mansion — and their original features, from stately columns and stone archways to ceiling frescoes and tiled courtyards, remain rich with character, even while the interiors have been updated in a crisp modern-classic style.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Gran Hotel Inglés in Madrid
ld.description: Once the neighborhood of Miguel Cervantes and other titans of Spanish letters, Madrid’s Barrio de las Letras is also home of Gran Hotel Inglés, the city’s oldest luxury hotel, welcoming guests since 1886. It’s unassumingly tucked away on the narrow, brick-laid Calle de Echegaray, and in its modern incarnation it styles itself an urban oasis — hence the Sisley spa. The interiors, by New York’s Rockwell Group, pay tribute to the Art Deco era, with brass accents, geometric ornaments, and rich, dark hardwood floors, along with custom textiles, lamps, and furniture. The glamorous lobby bar, with sleek leather stools arranged around a circular marble counter and a dramatically illuminated liquor shelf suspended from the ceiling like an art installation, makes a striking first impression — and in a concession to the steady stream of madrileños passing through for drinks, there’s plenty of space nearby to relax with a gin and tonic on a Chesterfield sofa or a velvet armchair.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Caro Hotel in Valencia
ld.description: Valencia’s Old Town has some fine historic hotels, but perhaps none as notable as this one, set in a 14th-century Gothic palace that served as the private mansion of the Marquis de Caro. It’s the city’s only historical monument hotel, and Caro Hotel leans into the official designation, proudly showcasing a 12-century Arabic wall in its restaurant and medieval coffered ceilings and Moorish archways in the guest rooms. The otherwise modern and minimalist design, with monochromatic decor and sophisticated lighting, evokes the stage-like atmosphere of a contemporary art gallery — all the better to let the building’s historical elements shine. The chic library and multiple outdoor terraces, one with a plunge pool, add to the appeal, as does Xanglot Restaurant, a striking restaurant where both the design and the cuisine take inspiration from the city’s Roman, Arabic, and Christian roots.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Puntagrande  in El Hierro
ld.description: The Guinness Book of World Records officially designated Hotel Puntagrande in El Hierro, Spain as the world’s smallest hotel in 1984. But what’s especially notable about this “hotelito” isn’t its small size, but its spectacular location on a piece of lava rock jutting out into the Atlantic Ocean. The original building, a cultural site protected by the Canary Islands government, dates back to 1830. Inside, the hotel looks something like a small nautical museum, its rough-hewn stone walls lined with antique compasses, maps, and bronze-plated boat registrations.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Plaza de la Trinidad, Esquina Buensuceso 2

ld.name: Seda Club Hotel in Granada
ld.description: From its location in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada mountains to its world-renowned medieval architecture, Granada is a city celebrated for its beauty and history. And, while the Seda Club Hotel has an ideal location in the heart of the historical center just steps from the Cathedral, there’s nothing old-fashioned about it. The 21 rooms and suites share a contemporary, slightly Art Deco feel with jewel-toned accents and herringbone wood floors, while the bathrooms are especially sparkly, with tiled walls and floors winking at the nearby Alhambra. The Seda Club restaurant frames views of the Plaza de la Trinidad, and the cocktail bar is a swanky spot, but it’s the oasis-like rooftop that calls to guests at the end of a long day’s touring.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Palacio de los Ángeles in Haro
ld.description: After finding success with the TWO-MICHELIN-Star Venta Moncalvillo, the Echapresto Brothers have embarked on another project in Spain’s La Rioja wine region with the opening of Palacio de los Ángeles. The brothers have restored and transformed an 18th-century baroque palace into a collection of stylish and contemporary rooms and apartment-style residences and, unsurprisingly, oversee the menu of the relaxed restaurant themselves. They’ve also carefully curated the wine bar’s well-stocked cellar, which is home to the world's largest collection of Rioja Q.D.O. Wellness has also being thought about, with a small space dedicated to a gym, spa area, and beauty treatments.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Seaside Grand Hotel Residencia in Gran Canaria
ld.description: The Grand Hotel Residencia enjoys a prime location on the coast of Gran Canaria, sitting under leafy palms just a few minutes’ walk away from the sandy beach of Maspalomas. Attractive rooms come in sky blue shades with a mix of prints and textiles, dark wood four poster beds, and the highlight, balconies surrounded by lush greenery. The restaurant serves a Mediterranean-inspired menu with a particular focus on local ingredients; the fruit and vegetables for instance come from a nearby finca on the island. There’s also a pool bar for tapas, and in the evening, a piano bar for live music and aperitifs. The slow living, seaside experience is enhanced with some spa time, or for a more serious approach to wellbeing, the hotel can even organize physiotherapy. Golfers will also find five of the island’s seven courses close by the hotel, and plenty of other sports take place at sister address Seaside Palm Beach, which sits just next door, including tennis, yoga, and Tai Chi.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa Boutique 1880 in A Lama
ld.description: Sitting in the Galician village of Gaxate, the Swiss-designed Villa Boutique 1880 remained in the hands of three generations of the same local family before it was sensitively transformed into a hotel. To respect this heritage, individually designed rooms take their names and character from the building’s architectural details and family stories, but expect a mix of classic neutral shades, rustic beams, and original arched windows that look across the manicured gardens. It’s here you’ll find the outdoor heated pool, which can be complemented by a number of different yoga classes — Hatha, Vinyasa, and even Tog Chöd and Tibetan Sword Yoga — or with spa treatments that combine the relaxing properties of massage, aromatherapy and sound healing. The restaurant puts a contemporary riff on Galician flavors and produce with a seafood-driven menu and Spanish dessert favorites such as filloas, torrijas, and baked cheesecake.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Camino del Barranco por la Vegueta 24

ld.name: Hotel César Lanzarote in Lanzarote
ld.description: Sitting surrounded by nothing but sea and mountain views, the adults-only Hotel César Lanzarote is all about slowing down and switching off. Guest rooms take their cues from nature with layers of tactile materials in shades of blue and green, and plenty of leafy potted plants to bring the outside in. All rooms come with a mountain or sea view, and some come with a patio. There’s a restaurant and bar but really the facilities here are all about getting outdoors, either lounging around the infinity pool, enjoying the gardens and terrace, or dining al fresco in the picnic area. You can even cook up your own BBQ. The wellness offering includes yoga classes, a gym and soothing spa treatments, or get your fitness fix out in nature by hiking, biking, horseback riding, and golfing.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Arts Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: A hundred yards from the Mediterranean, Barcelona’s Hotel Arts was tied with the Torre Mapfre for the tallest building in Barcelona until the continued construction on Gaudí’s Sagrada Família placed the church just a couple of meters higher, knocking both down to joint second place. Even without the accolade this 44-floor skyscraper is a striking feat of architecture, its inside-out steel superstructure gleaming in the sun.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sa Creu Nova Petit Palais in Mallorca
ld.description: When it comes to Mediterranean escapes the Balearic island of Mallorca isn’t exactly obscure. But there are places on this island where you can still get away from it all. The town of Campos, in the island’s southeast, is one of these places. It’s less than a half-hour’s drive from the spectacular Es Trenc beach; and, more to the point, it’s the home of Sa Creu Nova Art & Spa.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: ABaC Restaurant & Hotel in Barcelona
ld.description: Barcelona, already one of Europe’s hottest destinations, has in recent years consolidated its position as a worldwide culinary capital. It’s no longer just about tapas bars that stay open long after other countries have gone to bed, it’s about cutting-edge culinary experimentation as well, pushing high-end dining beyond its traditional limits. And so we see hotels like the Àbac Restaurant Hotel, hotels that quite literally put the restaurant first.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Son Brull in Mallorca
ld.description: The Spanish island of Majorca caters to both club-hopping oblivion-seekers and more tranquil, restorative holidays. A former 18th-century Jesuit monastery given new life as a rural boutique, farm, and vineyard in that sweet spot between the Tramuntana mountains and the Bay of Pollenca, is clearly oriented toward the latter. At Son Brull Hotel & Spa you can leave the dancing shoes at home, and soak in the serenity.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Urbanización Atalaya de Canyamel, Vial A, 12

ld.name: Cap Vermell Grand Hotel in Mallorca
ld.description: Mallorca might be an island paradise, but its’s hardly out-of-the-way: by boat or plane, it’s just a hop, skip, and a jump away from Barcelona. It’s a big island, one that brings in steady waves of tourists, and its hospitality scene has grown to meet demand, which is now enough to sustain a top-flight luxury resort like the Cap Vermell Grand Hotel.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Ritz, Madrid in Madrid
ld.description: More than a century after its founding by the legendary hotelier César Ritz, this Belle Époque palace remains central to the Spanish capital’s hospitality scene. And though it’s now a member of the Hong Kong–based luxury chain, Mandarin Oriental Ritz, Madrid is still one of a kind. Its location, within the Golden Triangle described by the city’s most famous museums, is as auspicious as they come — it helps that King Alfonso XIII was instrumental to its establishment — and the architecture, both inside and out, is nothing short of monumental.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental, Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: Some gleaming, towering modernist glass monolith just wouldn’t play in lovely, historic Barcelona. That’s why the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona makes its home where it does, in a classic bank building that’s the better part of a century old. The stately facade blends well with its tony Eixample surroundings on the Passeig de Gràcia, although inside the hotel follows Mandarin Oriental’s typically contemporary design codes.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Maria Cristina in San Sebastian
ld.description: We're as fond as anyone is of the small hotel, the quirky hotel, the independently owned, off-the-beaten-path hotel — but there's something to be said for seeing a city from the vantage point of one of its classic grand hotels. San Sebastian's most luxurious hotel is the Hotel Maria Cristina, on the banks of the Urumea river, a massive Belle Époque mansion in the heart of the city, lovingly maintained and painstakingly restored.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Villa Magna in Madrid
ld.description: A former palatial residence divided into spacious apartments for Spanish counts and countesses, the Villa Magna made the transition to its current five-star status after an extremely thorough renovation. The modernist granite exterior might not be exactly what you expect from a royal residence, but at the Rosewood Villa Magna it’s the unobtrusive perfection of the meticulously designed interior that counts. Instead of a heavy, imposing brand of marble-clad luxury, the Villa Magna specializes in a sort of whispered opulence that makes this hotel the choice for visiting heads of state, celebrities, business travelers and tourists alike.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Hotel Marques de Riscal, a Luxury Collection Hotel

ld.name: Hotel Marques de Riscal, a Luxury Collection Hotel in Elciego
ld.description: Originally intended just as a corporate headquarters for the Marquès de Riscal, this distinctive Frank Gehry building proved to be too special not to share — so now it’s open to the paying public, as one of the most unique winery hotels in the world: Hotel Marques de Riscal.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Avenida Virgen de Guadalupe 21, Playa La Enramada, La Caleta 38679

ld.name: Royal Hideaway Corales Resort in Tenerife
ld.description: The Royal Hideaway Corales Resort is two hotels in one: the family-friendly Royal Hideaway Corales Suites and the adults-only Royal Hideaway Corales Beach. Both are stylish, spacious, and luxurious; they differ primarily in their atmosphere, the one lively and the other elegantly tranquil. The building and its design contrast sharply with the traditional fishing village that is La Caleta, but the resort feels perfectly suited to its location, overlooking the rooftops of the town, with the beach just steps away. There are plenty of options for recreation and fitness and for dining, there are nine restaurants across the two properties including four Michelin stars at Royal Hideaway Corales Beach with one star each for San-Hô and Il Bocconcino plus the two-Michelin-starred El Rincón de Juan Carlos.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Santa Catalina, a Royal Hideaway Hotel

ld.name: Santa Catalina, a Royal Hideaway Hotel in Gran Canaria
ld.description: Since opening its doors in 1890, the luxurious Santa Catalina has been a symbol of refinement in Las Palmas, playing host to the likes of Winston Churchill, Maria Callas, and the Spanish royal family. The oldest hotel in the Canary Islands is still one of the best, and extravagant renovations by the Barceló Hotel Group have put a new shine on the silver and a new polish on the marble. Some things haven’t changed: the hotel’s pale pink façade, a colorful Spanish art collection, a traditional English afternoon tea served in a wood-paneled salon. And while guest rooms and suites retain their compact original dimensions, they’ve been smartly refreshed. Added inducements include an oceanview infinity pool, a stylish rooftop bar, a state-of-the-art spa, and a one-MICHELIN-Star restaurant called Poemas.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Canfranc Estación, a Royal Hideaway Hotel

ld.name: Canfranc Estación, a Royal Hideaway Hotel in Huesca
ld.description: Its name is to be taken quite literally: Canfranc Estación, a Royal Hideaway Hotel is in fact a hotel occupying the beautifully preserved Canfranc International Station, a piece of railway history dating back to 1928 — an impossibly ornate edifice with the rocky mountainsides of the Aragonese Pyrenees as a backdrop. Its 104 rooms and suites are designed in a style that recalls the early 20th century, even though the comforts are thoroughly modern. There’s a substantial spa and wellness center — the building is certainly long enough for a lap pool — and its restaurant, Canfranc Express, has earned a Michelin star under the direction of chef Eduardo Salanova and manager Ana Acín.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Bahia del Duque in Tenerife
ld.description: It’s a lot to take in: a Spanish colonial-style village by the sea, an array of themed restaurants, the staff in traditional garb. But the Bahía del Duque is a classic, and for good reason. The region’s first-ever luxury resort sits on prime real estate, right on the sand in the Costa Adeje area on Tenerife’s south coast, and the original designers made the most of it; the grounds are gorgeous, with palm tree-lined paths weaving past oasis-like swimming pools and meticulously maintained gardens. Low-lying pastel villas house hundreds of light-filled rooms and suites, many with ocean views, as well as nine restaurants (including one with a MICHELIN Star), 14 bars and lounges, a 24-hour fitness center, a kids’ club, an observatory, and a sleek spa with an outdoor thalassotherapy circuit. More than 20 years since its grand opening, the Bahía del Duque still reigns over the Canary Islands’ ever-expanding hotel scene.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Esperit Roca in Girona
ld.description: There are a mere 45 seats and a long waiting list at one of the world’s most famous restaurants, El Celler de Can Roca, and the intimate dining experience is part of its appeal. It’s only logical that the enterprising owners — Joan, Josep, and Jordi Roca, respectively a chef, sommelier, and patissier — were open to expansion. Their new project, housed in a restored 19th-century fortress on a mountaintop outside Girona, features a second restaurant, as well as a stylish boutique hotel, the Hotel Esperit Roca.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Hotel La Caminera Club de Campo

ld.name: Hotel La Caminera Club de Campo in Torrenueva
ld.description: Luxurious accommodation in a farmhouse in rural La Mancha which is perfect for a relaxing stay. Facilities include a spa offering olive oil-based treatments, a golf course, a hunting ground, a winery and even a landing strip for private jets!

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Finca Victoria Hotel & Spa in Girona
ld.description: Just above Sa Riera beach in Begur, Finca Victoria is a restored Catalan villa turned relaxed seaside escape. Its rooms and suites feature natural textures: terracotta floors, lime-washed walls, and hand-thrown ceramics, with options like private terraces, outdoor showers, or plunge pools. Guests can unwind in the saltwater pool, book a hydrotherapy session at the spa, or settle in with a book in the shaded lounge. Meals draw from seasonal Catalan traditions, served across two sunlit dining spaces. It is the kind of place where everything is designed to feel easy, inviting, and memorable.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Fairmont La Hacienda Costa del Sol

ld.name: Fairmont La Hacienda Costa del Sol in Alcaidesa
ld.description: Fairmont La Hacienda anchors a lesser-known stretch of the Costa del Sol, between Sotogrande and La Línea. The resort spans nine hectares of landscaped grounds with sea-facing rooms and direct access to La Alcaidesa beach. Two championship golf courses offer views of Gibraltar and, on clear days, Morocco. Rooms and villas are spacious, with natural materials, soft tones, and private terraces throughout. It is a well-placed coastal base for golfers, families, and travelers looking for a slower pace on Spain’s southern coast.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rural Sant Ignasi in Minorca
ld.description: Just beyond Ciutadella, on a quiet stretch of countryside, Rural Sant Ignasi occupies a former 18th-century manor surrounded by native trees and dry-stone walls. Rooms feature natural stone, wood, and woven fibres, with garden terraces in some and wide countryside views in others. The setting is serene but rooted and everything, from the ceramics to the fabrics, reflects the island’s traditions. Several unspoiled beaches are nearby, and the historic center is just a short drive away. The estate also has a pool, tennis court, and shaded walking paths throughout the grounds.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Only YOU Boutique Hotel Madrid in Madrid
ld.description: Picture a stately 19th-century palace that’s been transformed into a boutique hotel, one that has everything going for it: a mix of old-world glamour and modern interiors by a prominent designer in an enviable address in the heart of Madrid’s hip Chueca neighborhood. Digest all of that before we tell you the next part. It’s called Only YOU Boutique Hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Predi Son Jaumell in Mallorca
ld.description: Near the east coast of Mallorca, just about as far as you can get from Palma, the capital, is Predi Son Jaumell, a 16th-century agricultural estate lovingly refashioned into a beautiful 24-suite luxury boutique hotel. The tranquil atmosphere and the modern-meets-historical style are among its strengths, and the contrast between the centuries-old house and the crisp contemporary interiors is indeed deftly managed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Carretera de Roses, Pau, Costa Brava Alt Emporda

ld.name: Hotel Mas Lazuli in Girona
ld.description: There’s more to Catalonia than just bustling Barcelona — Girona is a destination in its own right, the home of an ancient Roman citadel, medieval baths, and the largest Jewish quarter in Catalonia, just half an hour’s train ride away from the capital city. And 30 minutes from Girona, near the French border, is Hotel Mas Lazuli, a 17-room boutique housed in a historic convent that dates to the 11th century. Life is a little less frantic here — this is the sun-drenched Costa Brava, complete with historic landmarks and a slowed-down pace that encourages you to indulge in a siesta instead of squeezing in a visit to another museum.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Santo Mauro, a Luxury Collection Hotel

ld.name: Santo Mauro, a Luxury Collection Hotel in Madrid
ld.description: The Duke of Santo Mauro’s 1895 French-style neolassical mansion is now one of Madrid’s most elegant and luxurious hotels. At just 51 rooms, and located in a largely residential district off the Paseo de Castellana, it’s intimate—a feeling magnified by the discreet nature of the service. Any number of foreign dignitaries and stars of the stage and screen prefer the Santo Mauro, but as for names, the staff aren’t talking, and except for the Beckhams (hardly the world’s most discreet couple anyway), neither are the guests.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: VIVOOD Landscape Hotel & Spa in Alicante
ld.description: About an hour from Alicante, on the slopes of Guadalest Valley, stand a collection of ultra-modern glass-walled boxes, creating maximal contrast between the high-design interiors and the starkly beautiful landscapes outside. Vivood Landscape Hotel & Spa - Adults Only is a rare instance where the architects and the hoteliers are one and the same, so the design never fights against the hospitality, and function is never compromised in the name of form. In addition to what the name promises, Vivood includes a restaurant, one informed by the Slow Food movement and the modern appetite for farm-to-table organic cuisine.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: METT Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: METT Barcelona is a unique place, equal parts city boutique and luxury resort, located on a hilltop just outside of Barcelona. The view is stunning, overlooking the city, and beyond, the Mediterranean, and the location is secluded, a thousand feet above the city, yet with relatively easy access to any destination within thanks to the hotel’s free hotel shuttle service to Passeig de Gràcia.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Faustino Gran in Minorca
ld.description: Compared to busy Mallorca and the party mecca of Ibiza to the southwest, the island of Minorca sees precious few tourists. And that, of course, is the key to its appeal. Not that you’re going to isolated when you check into a place like Faustino Gran Relais & Chateaux: the 24-room boutique is located just across from the port of Ciutadella. It’s an older city than you’d think, serving as the island’s religious center since the fourth century, once governed by the Moors. Thanks to that age-old cultural confluence, the port city has a medina-like feel, the sort of place that’s made for wandering, drinking in the evening silhouettes and views over pristine white beaches and the clear blue waters beyond.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Alfonso XIII in Sevilla
ld.description: Hotel Alfonso XIII is a relic of a bygone age, in the best way — built in 1928 to anticipate the Ibero-American Expo the following year, the hotel was named for the then-current king, and constructed in a an opulent blend of Baroque and Moorish styles that looks centuries older. Of course in the thirties, everything changed — just ask Hemingway, W.H. Auden, or George Orwell — but at the Alfonso, it will always be 1929.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Palace, A Luxury Collection Hotel, Madrid

ld.name: The Palace, A Luxury Collection Hotel, Madrid in Madrid
ld.description: The Palace, A Luxury Collection Hotel, Madrid has been around since 1912, and has for decades been one of the most elegant hotels in a city full of grand old hotels. Madrid is a courtly city, built up around a government that moved here as a gesture of Spanish unification; thus servicing the aristocracy was long the only game in town.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Nobis Hotel Palma in Mallorca
ld.description: Bridging the old world and the new isn’t an easy feat. Try too hard to honor the past and you’ll end up with a museum, but forge ahead a smidge too far and it can feel soulless. But then there’s Nobis Hotel Palma, a boutique hotel with a fresh feel snuggled inside a 12th-century Muslim palace. The 37 rooms and suites display a hushed sophistication, where stone walls and wood floors are the foundation for a pared-down, Danish-inspired design. From the spa to the sun terrace, it’s all about relaxation at this Mallorcan gem. Multiple dining and drinking venues are present, none more dramatic than the Nobis Rooftop with its spectacular sunset views.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Castillo Hotel Son Vida, a Luxury Collection Hotel

ld.name: Castillo Hotel Son Vida, a Luxury Collection Hotel in Mallorca
ld.description: Luxury and classical style go hand in hand in this historic seigneurial property. It is situated amid leafy pine groves and boasts splendid views of the bay and mountains.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Room Mate Helen Berger in Valencia
ld.description: Though it’s set in the heart of Valencia, in a historical structure right next door to the city’s 600-year-old university, Helen Berger is no antique — this is a thoroughly modern boutique hotel, one that mixes period architectural details with modernist furniture and a pared-down, contemporary interior-design style. There’s a residential calm to the rooms, and a wide variety of sizes and layouts, from classic doubles to triples and even a pair of penthouses with outdoor terraces. The neighborhood offers plenty of entertainment but the hotel’s own all-day restaurant and bar is a very worthy option.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Seventy Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: It’s not easy to up the ante in a city this full of stylish hotels, but that’s just what Seventy Barcelona did when it opened its towering front doors in 2019. Its larger-than-life ambitions are visible from the street, just off the Passeig de Gràcia; peer through its floor-to-ceiling windows and you’ll see an airy modern lobby, an industrial-chic space that blurs the lines between bookstore, coffee shop, art gallery, and co-working venue. Indeed, it’s all of these, attracting a fashionable local clientele, though some of the hotel’s finest features — like the rooftop terrace with striped chaises and a lovely pool — are reserved just for guests.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mirlo Barcelona in Barcelona
ld.description: Unlike the majority of Barcelona’s luxury hotels, Hotel Mirlo Barcelona isn’t in the city center. “Mirlo” means “blackbird” in Spanish, the concept being that guests explore the city by day — about a 20-minute drive or metro ride away — and return to the nest when they please. In addition to greenery and tranquility, this stately villa-turned-hotel offers romantic but modern suites, each with private spa features (some combination of hammam, Jacuzzi, rainfall shower, hydromassage tub, and sauna, or in the case of the swish Suite Mirlo, all of the above). There are lots of places to relax, from gorgeous gardens and a quiet courtyard swimming pool to a cozy library and a sun-filled indoor-outdoor restaurant and bar. The only problem might be working up the energy to leave the place and head into the city. Luckily, Parc Güell, also outside the city proper, is just ten minutes’ drive away.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Four Seasons Hotel Madrid in Madrid
ld.description: Leave it to the Four Seasons to take four historic buildings and transform them into one sensational showpiece. This brand is synonymous with service and style, and the Madrid property is no exception. Here, landmark architecture and historical details seamlessly blend with contemporary panache, especially in the supremely elegant guestrooms and suites. Its city center location is a boon for those exploring Madrid by foot, while the spa and pool await for some downtime. The hotel’s extensive art collection features a number of rising Spanish artists; equally eye-catching is the view from the buzzing rooftop restaurant.
ld.petsAllowed: \n One pet 10kg and under per room is allowed. Additional charges apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

address.streetAddress: Avenida Louison Bobet 9, Urbanización Mijas Golf

ld.name: La Zambra Resort in Malaga
ld.description: After a thorough renovation this onetime haunt of the likes of Princess Diana and the Rolling Stones is back as La Zambra Resort. The name refers to a regional form of flamenco, and while there’s no mistaking that the current iteration for anything but a Hyatt, the hotel has a sun-dappled, free-spirited air that’s true to its origins. Step through the gates into a cloister-like compound with airy white courtyards, elegant archways, gurgling fountains, and stately palm and cypress trees. There’s calm and quiet around the aquamarine pools, in the earth-toned suites with views of the mountains and the surrounding golf course, even over tapas and sunset drinks at one of several restaurants and bars overseen by a chef from San Sebastián. It’s the kind of place anyone, rock star or not, would be pleased to disappear for a few days.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sofitel Barcelona Skipper in Barcelona
ld.description: Sofitel Barcelona Skipper reopened in 2022 after a full transformation, bringing French luxury to Barcelona's beachfront at a surprisingly reasonable price. Maritime-themed interiors run throughout: royal blue and white with Gaudí-inspired flourishes that bridge Paris and Catalonia. Two pools split the difference: a family-friendly ground-floor option and a smaller rooftop setup with panoramic Mediterranean views and a DJ spinning most afternoons. Tendiez restaurant serves Spanish staples alongside French technique, made with local ingredients. Somorrostro beach is a three-minute walk. For Barcelona, beachfront hotels this close to the center remain rare.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Only YOU Hotel Valencia in Valencia
ld.description: It would be difficult for a hotel to be any more centrally located than Only YOU Hotel Valencia, which is set just a few steps from the Plaça de l’Ajuntament and a few more from the city’s cathedral. And despite its name, it’s more a tribute to its city than to its guests — a high-end boutique hotel with a bit of architectural history and some public spaces that aim to bring the locals and the guests into direct contact. Salvaje, the ground-floor restaurant, serves a Japanese fusion cuisine, while the top-floor El Mirador is a classic Valencian bistro.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Helguera Palacio Boutique & Antique in Santander
ld.description: Nestled in the foothills of Spain’s Pasiego Valley, this 17th-century palace captures the elegance of another era. Helguera Palacio, weighing in at a mere 11 rooms, invites a privileged few to slumber in sophistication, in an atmosphere of antique elegance and modern style crafted by interior designer Malales Martínez Canut. It’s surrounded by 14 acres of gardens and parkland, and features an indoor-outdoor pool with views of the landscape, as well as an impressive little spa and wellness center. Trastámara, the hotel’s fine dining restaurant, features a tasting menu focused on Cantabrian flavors as well as its own signature wine.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Finca La Donaira in Montecorto
ld.description: Finca La Donaira is more than a hotel — it’s also a working organic farm, a high-end stable dedicated to Lusitano horses, and a collection of active experiences scattered about its extensive Andalusian grounds. It sums up the southern Spanish good life rather neatly, and on a firmly eco-conscious foundation. The restored farmhouse shelters nine individually decorated rooms, each furnished with tasteful antiques and an intoxicating medley of weather-worn stone, reclaimed wood, adobe, and luxe textiles.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Four Seasons Resort Mallorca at Formentor

ld.name: Four Seasons Resort Mallorca at Formentor in Mallorca
ld.description: On Mallorca’s northern cape, Four Seasons has reawakened a legend. Formentor once drew writers, royals, and romantics to its quiet pine groves and silver beach, today the mood remains intact. Interiors by Gilles & Boissier are warm, tactile, and sea-facing, with travertine, raffia, and ochre-washed light throughout. Some suites come with private pools; all come with stories. Guests float between shaded terraces, soft-water swims, and tapas at the beachfront chiringuito. Everything’s been rethought except the view, which never needed changing.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets 25 lbs / 11.5 kg or less are permitted. Exceptions to the pet weight allowance may be made at the property level and / or for guests who rely on an animal for assistance. Charges apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Son Bunyola Hotel & Villas in Mallorca
ld.description: Son Bunyola carries centuries of history, and nearly three decades of anticipation. Richard Branson first bought this 16th-century Mallorcan finca in the ’90s, sold it, then finally brought it back to life in 2023. Positioned across 1,300 acres of terraced hills, olive groves, and UNESCO-listed coastline, the estate includes a 13th-century tower, a chapel-turned-restaurant, and a spa in what was once the old oven. Rooms are calm, spacious, and understated, shaped by local craftsmanship and Mallorcan character. It is a rare glimpse of the island’s wilder, more timeless side.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Gran Marbella Resort & Beach Club in Marbella
ld.description: The Gran Marbella Resort & Beach Club shows off a quieter side to glitzy Marbella. The beachside hotel offers natural garden, sea and mountain views from its elegant and contemporary rooms and suites, many of which come with luxurious extras such as private pools or Jacuzzis. And there are numerous laidback spots to eat and drink, including a beach club for dining with a sea view and private beach access. Even more relaxing is the spa, which comes with a huge indoor pool in addition to the sun-soaked outdoor pool, a Jacuzzi, hammam, cold plunge pool, and treatments courtesy of British brand Champneys.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Neri in Barcelona
ld.description: Neri feels like a secret hideaway tucked away in Barcelona’s Gothic Quarter. Just 28 rooms are housed across two historic buildings, including a 12th century medieval palace, and come with views across the Gothic quarter and Plaça de Sant Felip Neri, where Neri’s restaurant enjoys the privilege of being the only one in the square. There are also six apartments if you’re looking for even more privacy. Up on the rooftop the views continue from the small outdoor pool, bar and terrace.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

address.streetAddress: Calle de Diego de León, 43, Salamanca

ld.name: Heritage Madrid in Madrid
ld.description: Madrid has a long history of fine hotels, both grand luxury hotels and stylish boutiques; the two threads come together in the 48-room Heritage Madrid, occupying a stately townhouse in the upscale Salamanca district. The style melds century-old architecture and antiques with contemporary luxury design and first-rate modern comforts, and the restaurant, Haroma, is headed by the well-known local chef Mario Sandoval.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Dunas de Formentera in Formentera
ld.description: Dunas de Formentera melts into dune topography, just meters from the Mediterranean. Rooms strip back to sand tones and raw materials: wood, linen, raffia, with concrete bathrooms and Mortex fixtures. No televisions interrupt the sea view. The infinity pool mirrors the ocean's gradient blues.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Punta Negra, Mallorca in Mallorca
ld.description: Next to the luxe waterfront development that is Puerto Portals, a short distance outside of Palma, Mandarin Oriental Punta Negra stands watch over the Bay of Palma. It’s a bit of a stylistic departure for the brand, based as it is on an existing structure, which has been thoroughly renovated and greatly expanded. Still, the hotel weighs in at just over 100 units, lending it an almost boutique-like air of exclusivity.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. No extra charges.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Vestige Son Ermità in Minorca
ld.description: On a hilltop estate in northern Menorca, Hotel Vestige Son Ermità is set within centuries-old farm buildings of sandstone and limewash, where original wooden beams frame calm, earthy interiors. Rooms and suites balance rustic character with bespoke furnishings, some adding fireplaces, terraces, or garden views. The estate itself spans 800 hectares of farmland, orchards, and coastal trails that lead down to Cala Calderer. Produce from the groves and gardens finds its way to the seafood restaurant, while an outdoor pool looks across the countryside. Guests can also shuttle to sister property Binidufà for plant-based dining.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Schloss Elmau Luxury Spa Retreat & Cultural Hideaway

ld.name: Schloss Elmau Luxury Spa Retreat & Cultural Hideaway in Elmau
ld.description: Come winter, Schloss Elmau finds itself immersed in the kind of snowy wonderland that the Swiss might like to believe they’ve got exclusive rights to. But from the name of the place you can tell it’s a slightly different sort of ski hotel — it’s not every alpine resort that can credibly claim to be a “cultural hideaway.”

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Hotel Orania.Berlin in Berlin
ld.description: Originally intended as an office building in 1912, the building that now houses the Orania.Berlin survived the destruction of two world wars to emerge as a classic remnant of old Berlin in the city’s hip Kreuzberg neighborhood. Designed by hotelier Dietmar Mueller-Elmau, owner of the famous Schloss Elmau in the Bavarian Alps, and operated since 2017 by Jennifer and Philipp Vogel, the Orania reveals a level of luxury that surpasses what you’d expect from a Kreuzberg boutique hotel.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed at Hotel Orania.Berlin for 52.50 EUR per stay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: HOTEL ZOO BERLIN in Berlin
ld.description: In a way, the phrase “a new spin on an old classic” sums up just about everything that’s cool in Berlin. Not that that’s a criticism. They’ve got such great raw material to work with, there’s no sense beginning from a blank slate. Any hotelier, for example, would be thrilled to have something as monumental as Hotel Zoo to work with. A nineteenth-century mansion converted into a luxury hotel in 1911, it played host to many of the twentieth century’s leading lights, before beginning a slow fade into obscurity.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Traube Tonbach in Baiersbronn
ld.description: Anyone expecting doom and gloom from the Black Forest, in southwestern Germany, is in for a surprise. For one thing, it’s not black so much as green, a lush landscape filled with ancient forests and emerald grasslands. And though the name lends itself to some spooky connotations, a place like the Hotel Traube Tonbach is a reminder that a Black Forest holiday can be bright, airy, and filled with natural light.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are welcome, but only in rooms in the house Kohlwald.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Landhaus Stricker in Sylt
ld.description: In principle there’s a stark contrast between Landhaus Stricker’s thoroughly traditional exterior and its colorful, contemporary interiors. But in actual fact, the modern elements and the heritage architecture blend harmoniously together; the result is not only one of Sylt’s most handsome small hotels, but one of the most memorable in all of Germany.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed at a supplement of 25€ per day.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Der Birkenhof Spa & Genuss Resort in Neunburg v. W. – Hofenstetten
ld.description: The Obendorfer family has been looking after guests here with great commitment for more than 30 years. The beautiful countryside surrounding the hotel, the comfortable and elegant guestrooms and spacious modern suites as well as the spa facilities leave nothing to be desired! Whisky enthusiasts will be attracted to the hotel bar, and restaurant Obendorfers Eisvogel is the proud custodian of a pair of MICHELIN Stars.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Das Stue in Berlin
ld.description: Hotels these days have a few problems in common; among them, all too often, is a distinct lack of grandeur. It’s not the sort of thing that springs naturally from what is typically little more than a box, jammed with as many beds as it can reasonably hold. That’s why, if it’s grandeur you’re after, you might be better off converting an existing building into a hotel, rather than building your own bedbox from the ground up. Das Stue, in Berlin’s Tiergarten district, is a case in point. This Thirties embassy building was built, at least in part, to convey a grand impression — and its atmosphere, after a massive architectural overhaul by Annette Axthelm and an interior renovation by the renowned Spanish designer Patricia Urquiola, is about as far as you can get from the boxes-and-boxes sameness of the typical contemporary hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Telegraphenamt in Berlin
ld.description: This neo-Baroque telegraph office was built back in 1910, in an era when even utilitarian industrial structures were expected to serve a partly ornamental purpose. And today this landmark has been put to a use that brings it into more direct contact, inside and out, with the public. Hotel Telegraphenamt Berlin, or HTA for short, benefits from a central location in Mitte, a few minutes’ walk from Museum Island, and its style, which freely mixes stark bare brick and exposed girders with Deco flourishes and classic modernism, is perfectly emblematic of the historic patchwork that is present-day Berlin.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Althoff Seehotel Überfahrt in Rottach-Egern
ld.description: With an alpine backdrop that could easily launch a thousand postcards, Lake Tegernsee in Upper Bavaria is a stunning year-round destination for hikers, bikers, skiers and beer worshippers. Catering to well-traveled, wellness-oriented guests, Seehotel Überfahrt is more than just its stunning lakefront location. There’s not a shred of Bavarian kitsch to be found. Instead there’s a surprisingly vibrant streak running through the mod-luxe proceedings. Private balconies offer panoramic lake or mountain views, so everybody wins.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Schlosshotel Münchhausen in Aerzen
ld.description: Commissioned in 1570 by Hilmar von Münchhausen, this Weser Renaissance castle was once a gathering place for aristocrats, thinkers, and collectors. Today, Schlosshotel Münchhausen stands as a meticulously restored estate just outside the medieval town of Hamelin, set within landscaped parkland. Vaulted ceilings, parquet floors, and museum-worthy antiques depict its layered past, while multiple dining venues, two golf courses, and a serene spa define its present. It is a historic estate reimagined with poise, purpose and centuries of character.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Alpenloge Hotel in Scheidegg
ld.description: There’s something pleasingly symmetrical, even geometrical, about the design-focused boutique hotel Alpenloge.
