It’s located at the junction of four countries — Germany, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, and Austria — and each of its nine rooms is named after the cardinal direction it faces, some overlooking dazzling alpine landscapes and others a scenic mountain village. The architecture is loosely modeled after the Bavarian schoolhouse that once stood in its place, with a wood-shingled roof and high-ceilinged rooms bathed in natural light. But the interiors are more modern than traditional: the owners went to great lengths to outfit the interiors with the finest furnishings available in Europe, from king-sized beds by the renowned German manufacturer Schramm to chairs by Danish brands like Nor11 and Fredericia.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Relais & Châteaux Hardenberg BurgHotel in Nörten-Hardenberg
ld.description: Located at the foot of the Hardenberg castle ruins, a thousand-year-old clifftop monument that rises up majestically in the Palatinate Forest, Relais & Châteaux Hardenberg BurgHotel has a privileged location on the grounds of an ancient estate. The noble family abandoned the castle in the 18th century, around the same time the hotel was built — but the old distillery, tavern, and castle park are still in operation, and Hardenberg BurgHotel is the perfect base from which to enjoy them. With its red-shingled roof and half-timbered gables, the beautifully restored building exudes fairytale charm, and inside, it’s refined but cozy, with native wood flooring, exposed stone walls, and antique furnishings.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are welcome in specific room types and can be arranged at an extra supplement.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Strandhotel Dünenmeer - Adults only in Dierhagen
ld.description: The Baltic seaside resort town of Dierhagen Strand stands at the base of the Fischland-Darß-Zingst peninsula, noted for its beaches and nature reserves. And among Dierhagen Strand’s greatest strengths as a travel destination is Strandhotel Dünenmeer, a wellness-focused luxury resort surrounded by an idyllic landscape of forests, dunes, and white sand beaches.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Florentin by Althoff Collection  in Frankfurt
ld.description: The Florentin began its life as Villa Speyer, a 1901 mansion belonging to a prominent local family. Later, as the Villa Kennedy, it was one of Frankfurt’s favorite luxury hotels, and gained its contemporary additions. Today, under the direction of the Althoff Collection, it’s been thoroughly reimagined as an urban retreat, oriented around an improbably tranquil central courtyard.
ld.petsAllowed: Dogs are allowed (€60 per night). No other pets are permitted

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sofitel Frankfurt Opera in Frankfurt
ld.description: The main focus of the Sofitel Frankfurt Opera is clearly stated in the name; it’s set not just in the Opera District, but right on the Opernplatz itself, just across the road from the newly rebuilt Alte Oper. But this is a fantastic location for business travelers as well — it’s also the central business district, with the historic city center a short walk in the other direction. Local color, then, is a given; this Sofitel, like all its siblings, emphasizes its Frenchness, both in style and in atmosphere.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Franks in Oberstdorf
ld.description: German hoteliers have always excelled at wellness-oriented rural escapes, and the Allgäu’s Frank family is no exception. In Oberstdorf, at the foot of the Alps, Hotel Franks is a classic of the genre — one that’s been updated for the 21st century, but that nevertheless retains the timeless appeal of the classic mountain lodge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Mandala Hotel in Berlin
ld.description: In the heart of Berlin’s Potsdamer Platz, surrounded by futuristic skyscrapers and modern architecture, is The Mandala Hotel, a tranquil oasis with views over the quiet inner courtyard, and balconies and terraces that take in the panorama of the city and the Tiergarten Park.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bayerischer Hof Munich in Munich
ld.description: There are a few grand hotels that stand somehow apart from all the trends that come and go in the hospitality world, and among them is the Bayerischer Hof Munich. This former royal palace became a hotel in 1841, and has been owned and operated by the Volkhardt family since 1897; its plans are quite literally measured in centuries.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Excelsior Hotel Ernst in Cologne
ld.description: Long Cologne’s number one grand hotel, the Excelsior Hotel Ernst has presided over Cathedral Square since 1863, a fixture in the heart of the city center. Over the last century and a half the stately old building has hosted all manner of VIPs passing through Cologne, from statesmen on down, and today finds it very much in fighting form.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Brenners Park-Hotel & Spa in Baden-Baden
ld.description: Baden-Baden is well-known as a spa, resort and convention town, and since 1872 Brenners Park-Hotel & Spa has been its finest hotel. This is a side of Germany that is often overlooked: here, at the edge of the Black Forest, one may indulge in all the finest creature comforts life has to offer, from the French-inflected cuisine to the healing effects of the thermal baths.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Landhaus Flottbek Boutique Hotel in Hamburg
ld.description: Gross Flotbek, in the western suburbs of Hamburg, is a mere 15 minutes via the S-Bahn from the bustling port city, and yet it feels a world apart. This was Denmark once, if you can believe it — and while the 200-year-old farmhouse complex that’s home to Landhaus Flottbek doesn’t date back quite that far, it’s nevertheless inspired by the traditions of Scandinavian hospitality. Hygge, the restaurant and bar, is the most visible example, named as it is for the untranslatable (but coziness-adjacent) concept that is Denmark’s most recognizable contribution to the world of hotels.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Esplanade Saarbrücken in Saarbrücken
ld.description: There was a time not so long ago when we wouldn’t have expected a city of Saarbrücken’s size, as appealingly cosmopolitan as it is, to be furnished with a boutique hotel of this caliber. But in the 2020s, you never know where you’re going to find a hotel like Esplanade. It’s a charming 19th-century school building on Max Ophüls Square in the atmospheric Nauwieser district, just to the east of the riverside town center.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed for 30 Euro per pet per day.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: RIVA - Das Hotel am Bodensee in Konstanz
ld.description: There’s plenty of scenic shoreline around Lake Constance — known as the Bodensee in German — one of the largest lakes in central Europe. Arguably the loveliest stretch is in the foothills of the northern Alps near the Swiss border, where the medieval city of Konstanz rises up on the waterfront. RIVA occupies one of the stately Art Nouveau villas on the lakeside promenade, and while the boutique hotel blends in with its surroundings, it’s been expanded and fully reimagined inside. The sleek, mostly white interiors, flooded with natural light, are reminiscent of a modern art gallery, while up on the rooftop, an ethereal outdoor pool, heated year-round, has dazzling views over the water.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Patrick Hellmann Schlosshotel in Berlin
ld.description: Located on a verdant, tree-lined suburban street, the only thing that distinguishes Patrick Hellmann Schlosshotel Berlin from the other mansions in Grunewald is a small sign lit subtly in white lights. Not surprisingly, it started out as a private residence in 1914: Walther von Pannwitz, the original owner, was a personal advisor to the Kaiser Wilhelm and as fervent a patriot as he was an art collector and attorney. Subsequent renovations — as expected, by Patrick Hellmann — split the difference between reverent Bavarianism and sleek contemporary poise. Don’t worry, the glass chandeliers, plush red rugs, and pop-eyed Prussian portraits still have their say; nevertheless, the place maintains a glittering present-day ambience, neither gaudy nor intimidating despite the surplus of gold leaf.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed (medium sized dogs)(charges apply).

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Wilmina Hotel in Berlin
ld.description: A former courthouse and women’s prison in Charlottenburg is the unexpectedly gorgeous raw material for Wilmina, a boutique hotel whose renovation leaves much of its original detail intact, but turns its atmosphere 180 degrees from its original purpose — and the sheer welcoming tranquility of the place is similarly the polar opposite of the edgy, confrontational approach favored by many other Berlin boutique hotels.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel München Palace in Munich
ld.description: These things do tend to move in cycles, don’t they? At one point, some years ago, the classic luxury hotel was something that desperately needed rebelling against. But now, with hoteliers the world over embracing modern design at its most outré, conservatism has itself become one of the last remaining forms of rebellion. And where better to turn for an immersion in classic comfort than the Bavarian capital, and the aptly named Hotel München Palace.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are welcome. There is a nightly €25 charge per dog.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Château Royal Berlin in Berlin
ld.description: From the exterior, it might look a bit more traditional than what you’d expect from a boutique hotel in the former East Berlin, but hotels like Château Royal are a big part of what makes this city perennially hip, and not just fleetingly fashionable. It’s made from a pair of historic buildings in Mitte, one from the mid-19th century and another from the early 20th, and its interiors are inspired by both eras, featuring herringbone parquet floors, handmade tiles, and other classic touches.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Burg Schwarzenstein in Geisenheim
ld.description: With its fairy-tale silhouette and its stone turret, Burg Schwarzenstein looks for all the world like a medieval castle. It was actually built in 1873 as a summer home for a German noble family and later transformed into a luxurious hotel with English-style gardens and sweeping views over the Rhine Valley. Seven rooms with period details — exposed stone, wooden beams, four-poster beds draped in silk canopies — are located in the main building and its castle tower, though most are housed in the modern Park Residence or the cottage-like Guest House a short stroll away. Castle restaurant serves regional specialities and the elegant Burgrestaurant, with its sunny terrace facing overlooking rows of vines, is the perfect spot for a glass of local Riesling.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. There is a surcharge of € 30 per night for pets.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Gasthof Zufriedenheit in Naumburg
ld.description: The medieval town of Naumburg was a big deal in the so-called High Middle Ages, a stop on a major trade route and home to an impressive cathedral which is, perhaps unsurprisingly, one of the town’s greatest attractions today. Against this rich historical backdrop, a little bit of contemporary design goes a long way; this explains the impact of Gasthof Zufriedenheit, a hotel whose 19th-century bones — practically a new build by local standards — were thoroughly renovated in 2016, resulting in something that’s subtly modern and surprisingly stylish, yet still in keeping with Naumburg’s deep roots.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa Sonnenhof Boutique Hotel in Bad Reichenhall
ld.description: Fans of the classic Alpine-lodge experience will have no difficulty satisfying their urges in Bavaria. But those travelers who see no contradiction between modern design and timeless mountain views will be grateful for a place like Villa Sonnenhof Boutique Hotel. It’s a minority opinion, perhaps, but it’s popular enough to keep Villa Sonnenhof’s seven rooms filled with appreciative guests.
ld.petsAllowed: This property doesn't accommodate pets.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sol'ring Hof in Sylt
ld.description: Just 15 rooms and suites are the extent of the accommodations at Söl’ring Hof, a high-concept oasis among the dunes on the northernmost German island of Sylt, a narrow, windswept spit of land with surprisingly restful beaches and a dreamy, easygoing lifestyle. Rooms adhere to a sundrenched, lightly nautical theme with cool-toned textiles, crisp contemporary lines, and terraces or fireplaces for the extra cozy touch. A small spa welcomes the weary traveler back from a barefoot beach jaunt; the hotel’s restaurant has been recognized with two MICHELIN Stars.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Seesteg Norderney in Norderney
ld.description: Set right on the beach in Norderney, with direct sunset-facing views over the North Sea, Seesteg is something unique: an 18th-century brick building, once a storehouse, now a thoroughly stylish luxury hotel. It’s a fairly substantial edifice divided into a mere 16 units in three categories: Loft, Studio, and Penthouse. Safe to say there’s nothing Standard about them. There’s a spa and wellness center as well as a heated outdoor infinity pool with a view that’s unusual for a German hotel, to say the least. And the finest feature might be the Michelin-starred restaurant, also called Seesteg.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are welcome for an additional fee.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Landhaus Wachtelhof in Rotenburg an der Wumme
ld.description: Rotenburg is one of those blink-and-you’ll-miss-it German villages dotting the countryside between Bremen and Hamburg, especially if traveling via the Autobahn. What a shame that would be given the likes of Hotel Landhaus Wachtelhof, an enchanted, turreted garden stay just steps from the forested trails of Lower Saxony. Just about every spot on the property enjoys bright views of the manicured landscaping, including the greenhouse-style winter garden and the armchairs by the fireplace in the lobby bar. Rooms complete the tranquil picture in local pine and Carrara marble, warm and welcoming after a hard day’s hike. Don’t forget to ask about their picnic baskets.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. There is a surcharge of € 15 per pet per night.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Adlon Kempinski in Berlin
ld.description: The first Hotel Adlon was opened at this site in Berlin Mitte in 1907, and immediately became the city’s most prestigious lodging. Kaiser Wilhelm II was an early and frequent guest, and during the teens and twenties European royals and American industrialists rubbed elbows with Chaplin, Einstein, and a then-unknown Marlene Dietrich. Greta Garbo met MGM’s Louis B. Mayer in an Adlon elevator, launching her American film career.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mandarin Oriental Munich in Munich
ld.description: Despite its distinctly old-fashioned appearance, this is, perhaps, Munich's most sophisticated hotel. Small and discreet, the Mandarin Oriental is still widely referred to by its old name, the Rafael, though this 19th century building was only converted to a hotel in 1990.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Althoff Grandhotel Schloss Bensberg in Bensberg
ld.description: Though the Grandhotel Schloss Bensberg is perhaps not the most conveniently located hotel for doing business in Köln, there’s more to life than convenience alone. This three-hundred-year-old Baroque castle, on a hilltop in Bensberg, twelve kilometers from the city center, is close enough that traveling downtown is no great trial, yet just remote enough that its old-world elegance and immersive luxury make for something of a resort experience, the kind of escape that’s hard to come by in a city hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Louis C. Jacob in Hamburg
ld.description: Hamburg’s Hotel Louis C. Jacob is the best of two worlds: an immaculately well-preserved historical hotel that’s also assimilated the lessons of today’s boutique-influenced luxury hospitality, and subtly modernized along the way. It starts with a lovely pair of buildings, one on each side of the Elbchaussee, the picturesque riverside drive to the west of the city proper. And it continues inside, where the hotel’s 19th-century Hanseatic elegance remains in full flower; its collection of artworks alone would be enough for a small museum.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten in Hamburg
ld.description: This impressive edifice has set the standard for luxury-hotel elegance in Hamburg since the late 19th century, a decade or so before the first Fairmont hotel was built. But in spite of the change of management, what’s now the Fairmont Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten has sacrificed none of its classic character.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Berlin in Berlin
ld.description: Berlin may be something of a byword for avant-garde international hipsterdom, but this is a city that can do stately and traditional with the best of them — and the Ritz-Carlton, Berlin is as emphatic example as you could ask for. The setting, in a skyscraper at the newly thriving Potsdamer Platz, makes it something of an emblem for the post-reunification era, but once you’re through its doors you’re struck by the timeless sensation that the Ritz-Carlton hotels so successfully create.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten Kempinski in Munich
ld.description: Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten Kempinski strikes that rare and resolutely German balance between venerable tradition and fastidious, tech-savvy modernism. Case in point: you'll marvel equally at the Pinakothek reproductions gracing the walls and the iPad in every room. Whether you’re booking spa treatments, exploring local cuisine or just in need of a spectacularly knowledgeable butler, you’ll find it all in easy reach from the comfort of your Ludwig II-era quarters. Not to mention the seasoned concierge team’s stellar reputation — these ladies and gentlemen are the very definition of proficiency and punctuality.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Fontenay in Hamburg
ld.description: Located on the shore of Alster Lake, the Fontenay allows easy access to Germany’s largest waterfront city, and lies within walking distance of the Kunsthalle, Bucerius Kunstforum museum, and the most fashionable neighborhoods. But it’s also the ultimate urban escape, which architect Jan Störmer described as his “Hotel in the Park.” Extensive amenities, such as an 8K jogging route, a two-MICHELIN-Star restaurant, and an indoor-outdoor pool with panoramic views make getting away from it all that much sweeter. Meanwhile, the 1,022-square-meter rooftop spa feels like a destination unto itself. And the rooms, with touchscreen room controls, walk-in closets, rain showers, and heated floors, are their own private retreats.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: La Maison in Saarlouis
ld.description: La Maison’s name gives its heritage away — this remodeled villa near the banks of the Saar is part of a region that has traded hands between France and Germany for centuries. Eclectic, design-forward details and artwork define the upmarket public spaces, while a new annex with extra guestrooms strikes a bold, minimalist architectural pose. Light-flooded rooms come with warm wood flooring, charming city views, and handsome boutique furnishings. The Two-MICHELIN-Star restaurant Louis is joined by a relaxed bistro, Pastis, and the chic gardens and terraces keep the experience grounded and fresh.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Kempinski Hotel Berchtesgaden in Berchtesgaden
ld.description: The location, set 1000m up with a backdrop of fantastic mountain scenery, is hard to beat, but the interior is also worth a look: harmonious chic and modern design made with top-notch materials. The penthouse duplex suites with roof terrace, for example, are first-rate, as is the spa. In addition to the Johann Grill restaurant, there is the sleek, elegant Two-MICHELIN-Star PUR. Tip: order a slice of Eckerbichl-Torte in the fireplace bar!

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Bareiss in Baiersbronn
ld.description: The storybook facades and evocative Black Forest backdrop make Hotel Bareiss a perennial favorite and regional mainstay. Over three generations, they’ve judiciously expanded the grounds and properties to form what amounts to a lusciously green estate with scaled-up resort amenities to match. The sheer variety of pools and saunas alone keeps the entire stay interesting. Elegant rooms benefit from touches of opulence like fresh bouquets, fireplaces, wainscoting, and piles of luxe linens.

award.awardFor: Three MICHELIN Keys · An extraordinary stay

ld.name: Grand Hotel Heiligendamm in Bad Doberan
ld.description: It’s not exactly tropical, but the Baltic is a sea all the same, and for the German aristocrats of the nineteenth century, Heiligendamm was the equivalent of a Cannes or a St. Tropez. In the intervening decades this paradise by the Baltic was rather overtaken by events; now, after a massive restoration project, Heiligendamm is back, with the Grand Hotel Heiligendamm leading the charge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Widmann's Löwen in Königsbronn
ld.description: The inspiration is pure classic mountain lodge, from the chalet-style main structure to the interiors decked out in blond wood and red fabric, but Widmann’s offers a thoroughly contemporary vision of the Swabian Jura. Its rooms are unmistakably modern in style, and while the two freestanding guest chalets are more rustic in their aesthetics, the experience is pure contemporary luxury. Widmann’s Löwen, the restaurant, is well known for its elevated take on the traditional flavors and recipes of the region.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: BUDERSAND Hotel – Golf & Spa - Sylt in Sylt
ld.description: The northernmost of Germany’s islands, Sylt is best known for its vast, sandy beaches. But one of its major attractions lies on the mainland-facing side. Budersand is home to an award-winning 18-hole links course, built in the Scottish style along the coast — and it’s also home to an impressively luxurious hotel. The crisp, contemporary rooms make the most of the sun and the sea views; all of them come with balconies facing either the golf course or the sea. An impressive spa is just as much a matter of course as several upscale restaurants, including the Michelin-starred restaurant KAI3 and a first-class bar.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Parkhotel Egerner Höfe in Rottach-Egern
ld.description: A relaxed and friendly establishment offering a successful mix of regional charm and modern elements with highly accommodating staff, all keen to play host. If you are looking for something a little special, book the Alm room. You will find upmarket suites and premium doubles in the Valentina and Catherina annexes.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Dollenberg in Bad Peterstal-Griesbach
ld.description: Some classic grand hotels have gone in for a full luxury-boutique makeover; others have modernized at a more measured pace. And some have gone out of their way to retain their original charm. Hotel Dollenberg was rebuilt in 1980 and renovated in 2011, but it remains absolutely true to its classic inspiration. It also remains refreshingly family-owned and -operated — all the more impressive given its status as one of the region’s most beloved lodgings.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel PURS in Andernach
ld.description: The ultimate in upmarket chic, this luxurious little boutique hotel with a very personal note bears the signature of designer Axel Vervoordt. The rooms in the 300-year-old main building are particularly charming. There is also an attractive bar where the à la carte breakfast is served every morning, and in the evening, reserve a table at the One-MICHELIN-Starred PURS NEW NORDIC JAPANESE CUISINE.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Der Öschberghof in Donaueschingen
ld.description: Der Öschberghof makes the most of the Black Forest’s natural grandeur, and offers much on site as well, with no fewer than three golf courses and a sprawling wellness complex. Rooms come in a sophisticated grayscale with private balconies to boot. A pair of MICHELIN Stars adorn the fine-dining restaurant, Ösch Noir.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

pages.h1: Hotel Villa Sorgenfrei & Restaurant Atelier Sanssouci

ld.name: Hotel Villa Sorgenfrei & Restaurant Atelier Sanssouci  in Dresden
ld.description: A lovely little avenue of beech trees leads up to this 18th-century manor house and former winery in Radebeul, a suburb of Dresden. They’ve worked hard to preserve its inimitable historic details dating back to the Zopf period, including murals, statuary, immaculate parkland, and a belvedere tower. 16 rooms and suites exude elegance with polished wood, sandstone, and oversized windows overlooking the gorgeous grounds. For something even more extraordinary, book the suite that comes with its own little garden.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Europäischer Hof Heidelberg in Heidelberg
ld.description: Heidelberg has an unusually high concentration of hotels, thanks in part to the landmark Heidelberg Castle, which attracts a million visitors each year. The city’s most luxurious hotel, Hotel Europäischer Hof Heidelberg, plays a part in that history: it first opened in 1865 to host aristocratic guests attending events at the nearby castle. Though it’s been expanded and modernized many times over, this grand old hotel has been run by the same family for over a century, and its elegant interiors — with rich woodwork, coffered ceilings, crystal chandeliers, heavy drapery, and period furnishings — evoke days gone by. Rooms and suites display a slightly more modern edge, featuring an ivory and gold color palette, dark wood flooring, linen duvets, brocade details, and a mix of antique and contemporary pieces. The hotel’s highlights include a light-filled indoor pool and rooftop sun deck and a retro-styled cocktail bar with wood-paneled ceilings and leather armchairs.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Rebstock Durbach in Durbach
ld.description: The Baumann family’s hotel, in a charming Black Forest setting, makes an ideal holiday home-from-home. The rooms are very comfortable and well-furnished. The beautifully designed garden with its quiet corners is another highlight.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Ritz-Carlton Wolfsburg in Wolfsburg
ld.description: High-tech industry and cutting-edge design are not perhaps the first things that come to mind at the mention of the words Ritz and Carlton. This one, however, is a bit different, with daring architecture, futuristic materials and some decidedly contemporary interiors, courtesy of none other than Andrée Putman, the grande dame of modern hotel design.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Severin's Resort & Spa in Sylt
ld.description: On the Wadden Sea side of the island of Sylt, facing back to the mainland, is the historic village of Keitum, home to a number of classic Frisian farmhouses as well as the luxurious Severin’s Resort & Spa, a modern 95-room hotel in an authentic local style. The rooms and suites are antique-influenced but beautifully contemporary, and full of up-to-date comforts, while the spa is elaborate even by German standards. And there’s a premium placed on food and drink, from the fine-dining Tipken’s by Nils Henkel to the more casual Hoog, accompanied by a bar, a cigar lounge, and a wine cellar equipped for private tastings.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Breidenbacher Hof Düsseldorf in Dusseldorf
ld.description: There’s a colorful backstory to the Breidenbacher Hof Düsseldorf, perched canalside on the city’s famed Königsallee boulevard. In its 19th-century heyday, this luxury hotel hosted dignitaries and Russian czars; the building was destroyed by bombs in World War II, rebuilt, then demolished again to make way for the glamorous current iteration. The elegant Lobby Lounge, with its coffered ceilings, dark wood paneling, and silk brocade, evokes the past, as do the retro brasserie, The Duchy, and the black marble bar. Rooms and suites are refined yet contemporary, featuring plush lounge space, spacious Italian marble bathrooms with deep soaking tubs, king-sized beds, and tech-forward bedside touch panels to control lighting and temperature. Downstairs, there’s a high-end spa with an indoor pool, two Finnish saunas, and a steam bath. While beneath street level, look for a portion of Düsseldorf’s old city walls on display, uncovered during a recent round of excavations.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Heinzler am See in Immenstaad am Bodensee
ld.description: Guests are looked after cordially and personally by the Heinzler family in this cosily appointed holiday hotel, which enjoys a quiet location by the lake. The hotel has its own boat jetty.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Spa & Golf Hotel Weimarer Land in Blankenhain
ld.description: Needless to say, the location on a 36-hole golf course is popular with golfers. No less appealing, though, are the upmarket guestrooms (our tip: the Wellness Suites) and the tasteful spa complete with pool with a view out onto the greenery, relaxation rooms and treatments. Cosy and elegant style throughout. Large playhouse and free supervision for children. Two eateries: the rustic GolfHütte (seasonal cuisine) and KornKammer (light bites).

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Die Sonne Frankenberg in Frankenberg
ld.description: A scenic stop on the Deutsche Märchenstraße, or German Fairy Tale Route, Frankenberg is known for its 500-year-old, ten-towered town hall. Right next door is Hotel Die Sonne Frankenberg, a luxury hotel housed in a trio of beautifully restored 16th-century buildings. Each has its own character — one was a brewery, one a wine shop, and another a civic auditorium — but they’ve been unified into one sophisticated property with modern suites, a spa, and several bars and restaurants, including one with a Michelin star.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Kronelamm im Schwarzwald in Bad Teinach-Zavelstein
ld.description: The dedicated hosts here offer a 1600-square-meter complex for wellness fans, comfortable rooms (including the Jungbrunnensuite), each with their own particularity, and a hiking lodge a kilometre’s walk away. Culinary options range from haute cuisine via the one-MICHELIN-Star Berlin Krone to Swabian specialities in the elegant Hotel Kronelamm im Schwarzwald.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Alter Meierhof in Heiligendamm
ld.description: Sure, it’s not the Maldives, but for a Baltic escape, a more conducive environment to wellness than that enjoyed by the Alter Meierhof Hotel could scarcely be imagined. Located on the German side of the Flensburg Fjord (Denmark is on the other side), the hotel occupies a quiet green spot adjacent to the water — one of the inlets of the Baltic Sea. A sandstone and half-timbered façade suggest that this is a centuries-old manor house, but a little probing reveals the Alter Meierhof was built in 1999 — so no gloomy corridors or plumbing issues here.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Alpenkönig in Oberstaufen
ld.description: The Bentele family runs a delightful hotel with high-quality, tastefully decorated guestrooms which are comfortable, elegant and decorated with pretty, modern details. There is also an attractive wellness area offering beauty treatments and spa facilities. The pleasant personal atmosphere of this hotel is guaranteed to make you feel at home.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Restaurant Spa Torkel in Nonnenhorn
ld.description: For four generations, the Stoppel family has been expanding and refining Hotel Torkel, which sits a five-minute walk from the northeast shore of Lake Constance, Germany. It’s a tidy suburban boutique that also boasts an attractive spa area for relaxation and creature comforts galore. Renovated rooms feature reclaimed wood and cozy textiles, and many have a Jacuzzi on the balcony. Roomy gardens and a heated outdoor pool round out the experience.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Cortiina Hotel in Munich
ld.description: Some high-design boutique hotels come on like your “cool” uncle, the one who’s wearing a lampshade for a hat by the end of Christmas dinner; so determined are they to be fun that it’s almost enough to put you off the very idea of fun for life. So it’s a relief when a hotel can be confident and visually striking without continually cracking jokes and trying hard to impress.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Roomers Berlin Steinplatz, Autograph Collection in Berlin
ld.description: Going back to 1913, the hotel now known as Roomers Berlin Steinplatz has always had a glamorous reputation, counting Vladimir Nabokov and Brigitte Bardot (separately, unless there’s a great story we don’t know about) among its famous guests. One hundred years later, the Art Nouveau landmark reopened as a sleek twenties-inspired boutique hotel, and one which is prompting visitors to venture outside the Mitte and book a room in a comparatively residential and artsy West Berlin neighborhood like Charlottenburg.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: The Charles Hotel, a Rocco Forte Hotel

ld.name: The Charles Hotel, a Rocco Forte Hotel in Munich
ld.description: Forget about Oktoberfest kitsch and the cliches of provincial Bavaria. Today’s Munich is a modern, cosmopolitan city — and it’s finally starting to get the modern, cosmopolitan hotels it deserves. It’s still a bit light on the funky little boutiques that a lot of us wish for, but The Charles Hotel means at least the high-end business/luxury guest will be well looked after.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Heidelberg Suites in Heidelberg
ld.description: Germany’s urban centers are magnets for hospitality experiments, for cutting-edge art and design. Heidelberg, by contrast, is a trip back in time. This is the Oxford of Germany, if you like, and the university, the churches, and Heidelberg Castle are exemplars of a long-ago Germany that’s vanishingly hard to find in the more modern cities. And it’s against this historical backdrop, in this most traditional of cities, that the Heidelberg Suites must be understood.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Das Kranzbach Hotel & Wellness Retreat in Kranzbach
ld.description: Das Kranzbach may be located an hour from Munich in the shadow of some of the most imposing peaks of the Bavarian Alps, but it’s not about rowdy tourists shedding their cold-weather gear in the hallways. This is a four-season wellness retreat, and while you can certainly take advantage of the region’s ample winter sports opportunities, the spa at Das Kranzbach offers much more than the average après-ski soak.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Gut Steinbach in Reit im Winkl
ld.description: Like many great independently run hotels, Gut Steinbach started as a passion project. In 2011, a German count purchased an aging hotel and its surrounding property, located on a high plateau in the Cheimgau region of the Bavarian Alps, and turned the place into a stylish mountain retreat. The scenic grounds are now home to a small organic farm where deer, chicken, and goats roam, and around the natural pond is a collection of sleek alpine chalets built by local craftsmen. The main building has been reimagined, too: lined in native wood and enormous glass panels, it houses a restaurant and fireplace bar, plus most of the hotel’s rustic-chic rooms and suites, where a cozy hunting-inspired aesthetic prevails. After hiking or skiing nearby, a striking spa with mirrored ceilings, exposed stone walls, and modern daybeds surrounding a large indoor pool is especially inviting.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Andaz Munich Schwabinger Tor in Munich
ld.description: Schwabing, one of Munich’s most upscale residential areas, is known for fashionable shops, sleek restaurants, and chic wine bars, and the Andaz Munich Schwabinger Tor fits in perfectly. The generously sized rooms have all the luxurious features you’d expect (and maybe some you wouldn’t), like black-out curtains, Illy coffee machines, floor-to-ceiling windows, and a complimentary mini bar with non-alcoholic drinks and snacks. With a popular steakhouse, hip café, and the city’s highest rooftop bar, this boutique-style luxury hotel has become something of a destination in its own right. Spa lovers will appreciate the two-story spa and fitness center, with its view over the Alps from the sundeck.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: BEYOND by Geisel in Munich
ld.description: A whole new concept from Geisel Private Hotels, this small hotel combines luxury and a "home from home". It offers an extremely central position, exclusive "bedrooms", a living room complete with library and an open-plan kitchen (serving breakfast and your favourite dish on request) as well as a 24hr concierge service – all included in the price.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Luisenhöhe - Gesundheitsresort Schwarzwald in Horben
ld.description: Luisenhöhe Gesundheitsresort Schwarzwald may have a mouthful of a name, but it essentially boils down to the restorative fundamentals of Black Forest resorts since time immemorial. It’s at the north end of Horben, a picturesque hamlet just over the Rhine from France, which gives every room a floor-to-ceiling panorama of foothills worthy of an Old Master. Floods of light fall on plenty of natural wood finishes in the rooms, which benefit from boldly patterned textiles and mid-century modern furnishings with an eco-conscious twist. Rounding things out is a sprawling wellness complex (hence the name), including a 25-meter heated pool and enough terraces to enjoy a different one every day.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Werdenfelserei in Garmisch-Partenkirchen
ld.description: Currently the place to stay in Garmisch, this all-wood hotel combining regional style, impressive attention to detail and a real touch of luxury lies on the edge of the Michael Ende Kurpark. Everything is tasteful and upmarket, some suites offer a private spa or open fire. For relaxing you’ll find a fantastic chill-out room under the steeply sloping roof, an all-year-round outdoor pool and the neun10 bar.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Rosewood Munich in Munich
ld.description: The first hotel in Germany for the venerable luxury brand, the Rosewood Munich is a modern hotel in a heritage building — or a pair of them, to be precise. Within the walls of the old State Bank of Bavaria headquarters and the grand old Palais Neuhaus-Preysing, right in the heart of old Munich, are some 132 rooms and suites, decorated in a timeless contemporary-classic style and outfitted with state-of-the-art luxuries. The Asaya Spa’s wellness offerings are thorough, and among the dining and drinking venues are Cuvilliés, a restaurant inspired by Alpine flavors, and the retro-styled Bar Montez.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Tortue Hamburg in Hamburg
ld.description: An opulent, modern and elegant design, from the lobby to the guestrooms and restaurants. Head to the Brasserie for French cuisine, or JIN GUI for Asian food. In addition, there is a magnificent courtyard, as well as the bars, which are a popular spot for hip after-work parties. Omnipresent throughout is the trademark tortoise (French tortue) in the form of statues, lamps, pictures etc.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Seezeitlodge Hotel & Spa in Gonnesweiler
ld.description: This spa hideaway lies on the picturesque Bostalsee lake close to the Saar-Hunsrück Nature Park and offers lovely spacious, modern rooms and an excellent all-in package including access to the stunning 5,000m2 spa complete with Celtic sauna village – what better way to get away from it all!

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Taschenbergpalais Kempinski Dresden in Dresden
ld.description: If you know your local history then you’ll know why a reconstruction of an 18th-century Baroque palace is just as big a point of local pride as an authentic, unreconstructed 18th-century Baroque palace. Either way, today the Taschenbergpalais is Dresden’s top luxury hotel, with the Kempinski flag flying over its 211-odd rooms and suites.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel / Weingut Meintzinger in Frickenhausen
ld.description: A hotel and winery in the Bavarian village of Frickenhausen, by the side of the Main river, this unique lodging is historically inspired but modern in its vision. Behind the heavy stone walls of the Hotel / Weingut Meintzinger lie 29 rooms that mix antique and contemporary elements, never shying away from modern colors and a bold graphic sensibility. There’s a well-equipped spa that’s as stylish as the accommodations, wine tastings are available, and a substantial breakfast is served in the dining room, which remains open all day for light bites and access to the public wine fridge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: JW Marriott Hotel Frankfurt in Frankfurt
ld.description: In buttoned-up, no-nonsense Frankfurt, a sculptural steel-and-glass tower of a business hotel is enough to stand out — though not too much. It helps that the JW Marriott Hotel Frankfurt also happens to be one of the city’s largest hotels, though in Germany’s financial capital, that sort of superlative is far less important than the fact that it’s about as functional, comfortable and well-run a business hotel as you’ll find, in Frankfurt or anywhere else.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Weissenhaus Private Nature Luxury Resort in Weissenhaus
ld.description: This luxury hideaway boasts 75ha of grounds with woodland and a natural beach, as well as an entire series of beautifully restored historic buildings including a palace! The guestrooms are stylish and individually designed (try the "Bathing Hut" for two), all decorated to the highest standard. Lovely spa, cinema and interesting food options.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Lieser Castle, Autograph Collection in Lieser
ld.description: Lieser Castle presides over a stretch of the lush, winding Moselle river in southwest Germany. Originally a 19th-century Italian Palladian villa, it’s since undergone a series of Art Nouveau renovations, a marriage that yields extraordinarily crafted detail at every corner of the edifice and the grounds. Make no mistake, this is gilded luxury — even the guestrooms go full wedding-cake, with crystalline chandeliers, wainscoting, sumptuous fabrics, and ornate furniture that would feature in museums elsewhere in the world. The hotel is perfectly positioned to explore nearby gems (Trier and Luxembourg are both within an hour’s drive) or the region’s famous white wine vineyards.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Das Graseck Mountain Hideaway & Healthcare in Garmisch-Partenkirchen
ld.description: Set in the mountains above Garmisch-Partenkirchen, and accessible only by cable car after parking up 500m away, Das Graseck is an illustration of the ease and expertise with which German hoteliers handle Alpine hospitality. The views are extraordinary, naturally, and the wellness program is particularly robust, handling everything from saunas to cancer screenings. An elevated Bavarian cuisine is served in abundance, from an expansive breakfast buffet to a four-course gourmet menu at Weingart’s. The rooms are contemporary, marrying classic Alpine pine wood with modern furnishings and up-to-date comforts.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Boutiquehotel Blaue Burg Falkenstein in Pfronten
ld.description: It’s an understatement to call Boutique-Hotel Blaue Burg’s location spectacular. Perched more than 4,000 feet above the fairy-tale landscapes of Bavaria, it’s set amid the peaks of the Allgäu Alps, right next to the oldest castle ruins in Germany. A fine dining venue has brought more traffic to the steep mountain pass in recent years, and since staying the night makes more sense than driving back down the mountainside in the dark, the property has expanded to include a stylish family-run boutique hotel.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Kulturhof Stanggass in Berchtesgaden
ld.description: The Berchtesgaden Alps have welcomed travelers of all sorts, from mountaineers, sanatorium residents, eco-tourists, and sports junkies to the Romantics of yesteryear. Rising from the ashes of an old-school luxury hotel, Kulturhof Stanggass instead fixes its gaze firmly on the future. Don’t worry, you’ll still get a knockout panorama of the Watzmann massif every morning — but you’ll also swap anecdotes over long tables and live music in the beer garden. There’s also the One-MICHELIN-Starred restaurant Solo Du. Take a bracing morning plunge in the natural pool, or finally dig into Thomas Mann in the stillness of your blonde-wood balcony. Clean, simple, healthy, eternal: let these be your bywords as you drink in nature’s magnum opus.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Bülow Palais in Dresden
ld.description: The Bülow Palais harmoniously integrates into Dresden’s Baroque Quarter. It promises exemplary service, upmarket, comfortable and individually designed rooms, and a wellness suite on the top floor. There is also an excellent breakfast, not to mention delicious cakes available in the afternoons.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Das Achental Resort in Grassau
ld.description: Between Salzburg and Munich, in the Chiemgau region of Upper Bavaria, between the Chiemsee lake and the Kampenwand peaks, is the town of Grassau, which is the setting for Das Achental, a perfect representative of modern-rustic Bavarian hospitality. The architecture retains its historical charm, while the rooms and suites update the classic materials with ultra-modern bathrooms and a contemporary design sense. An expansive spa and wellness program and an 18-hole golf course are among the diversions, while the culinary offerings include hearty classic Bavarian fare and a beer garden as well as a gastronomic restaurant worthy of three MICHELIN Stars.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Ketschauer Hof in Deidesheim
ld.description: Hotel Ketschauer Hof is just one component of a complex of boutique hotels, restaurants, and wineries in and around the small German town of Deidesheim. The Jordan family takes great pride in the region’s viticultural heritage, which informs the decor and exquisite antiques throughout its public spaces and the calming inner courtyard. The 18 rooms and suites preserve the eccentric layout of the historic building while updating the interiors with light-flooded, contemporary design cues.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Das Rübezahl in Schwangau
ld.description: A lovely quiet location, dedicated owners, comfortable elegant rooms (e. g. pretty themed suites), attractive spa with various saunas, outdoor pool, relaxation rooms, panoramic deck… Modern seasonal cuisine in the restaurant Louis II and a fantastic panoramic terrace. Plus, the AlpenRausch bar-lounge. You can even take a walk to the hotel's own mountain lodge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Landhaus Severin*s Morsum Kliff in Sylt
ld.description: Surrounded by the Morsum Kliff nature reserve, Landhaus Severin*s remote location means peaceful relaxation mixed with outstanding views. From the hotel’s terrace you can see clear out to the Wadden Sea. Needless to say, the location here is pretty tough to beat, but it’s more than matched by the interior design of this traditional thatched house, which is modern and tasteful with a touch of nautical Nordic.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Hotel Engel Obertal - Wellness & Genuss Resort

ld.name: Hotel Engel Obertal - Wellness & Genuss Resort in Baiersbronn
ld.description: Wellness & Pleasure Resort Engel Obertal is a meta-village of sorts; set within the Black Forest municipality of Baiersbronn and even more specifically the village of Obertal, it’s a self-contained and self-sustaining complex set on meadowlike, manicured grounds. It offers a balanced, well-paced life — enchanting forest hikes in the morning followed by a quick dip and sauna session, then a light meal at sunset with regional wines. Rooms nod to the area’s rich craft tradition with polished wood, floral accents, and earth-tone textiles. For more privacy and a luxe-rustic touch, go for the freestanding chalets — individual saunas and terraces are well worth the splurge.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Koenigshof, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Munich

ld.name: Koenigshof, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Munich in Munich
ld.description: Inside it’s an exploration of Munich’s contemporary, cosmopolitan side, and is as stylish as it is lavish. The art collection includes pieces by a number of well-known modern and contemporary artists; of particular note are the hotel’s spa and its highly regarded South American restaurant.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Das James in Flensburg
ld.description: Marina hotels and Germany aren’t an obvious combination, but Flensburg, at the end of a protected fjord, is an exception. And Das James is unusual even by local standards — its English name sets the tone for a hotel with a bit of country-house influence, as well as a strong current of urban loft style. The most basic rooms look out into a courtyard or garden, while the better ones face the marina and the harbor. Breakfast is served in the James Farmhouse restaurant, while Das Grace is the top-floor fine-dining restaurant, and the Lion the cozy English-style cocktail bar.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Strandhaus Spreewald in Lübben
ld.description: When Berliners need a break from the big city, they escape to the Spreewald, a fairytale forest dotted with quiet meadows and crisscrossed with canals. It’s possible to make it a day trip, but it’s more relaxing to stay over at a boutique hotel like Strandhaus Spreewald. This sustainably built hotel is set on a lush green landscape on the bank of the Spree River, and its design makes the most of it: an open-air beer garden and riverfront lawn offer ample outdoor lounge space, and many guest rooms have balconies or terraces with water views. Interiors are calming, with oak parquet floors, spa-like walk-in showers, and crisp white linens. Rent a paddleboat or a bicycle at reception to explore the Spreewald’s famous waterways and the charming town of Lübben.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Maison Messmer in Baden-Baden
ld.description: No place is more literally synonymous with spa culture than Baden-Baden, whose Royal Spa is a lavish and thoroughly modern tribute to the Roman baths that put this town on the map. Maison Messmer offers more than just bathing, of course — this is a lavish and not at all unstylish luxury hotel, whose ornately historical public spaces are complemented by crisp and contemporary rooms and suites.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Do & Co Hotel Munich in Munich
ld.description: The city-center building in which DO & CO Munich makes its home is an unusual one: FC Bayern World is a monument to the storied local football club, an immersive retail experience with contributions from partners like Audi and the DO & CO hospitality brand. The latter is responsible for a thoroughly tasteful and luxurious high-end boutique hotel, a worthy sequel to its older sister in Vienna. Along with 30 stunningly stylish rooms and suites — one for each of Bayern’s league championships to date — the hotel contains a pair of fine restaurants, one a contemporary Asian experience and the other an upscale Mediterranean-inspired bistro.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Mauritzhof Hotel Münster in Münster
ld.description: Münster is known for its Gothic architecture, and Mauritzhof Hotel Münster channels the dark beauty of the city’s churches. This design-focused boutique hotel’s aesthetic is moody and modern, done up in shades of slate gray, taupe, and turquoise, with lots of dark wood and glass and sleek midcentury furniture upholstered in rich fabrics like velvet and leather. Guest rooms are sleek and quiet, thanks to soundproofing, with parquet floors, feather beds, Nespresso machines, muted lighting, and bathrooms with underfloor heating, a welcome feature in winter. Some have balconies facing a skyline punctuated with towering church spires. Downstairs, have a martini by the fireplace or relax over lunch on the terrace before heading out to explore the bike-friendly city on two wheels.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Boutique-Hotel Friesinger in Kressbronn am Bodensee
ld.description: Take one lovely old villa and two restaurateurs with a dream of running their own hotel… What Dominique and Erik Essink have created is worthy of the name boutique hotel with its warm tones, fine fabrics and clean, modern lines.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Steigenberger Icon Parkhotel Düsseldorf in Dusseldorf
ld.description: You can tell the moment you enter the lobby! This is the Grande Dame of the Düsseldorf hotel scene, a real classic with a stylish modern touch, all of its guestrooms attractive and comfortable. Don’t miss Jones Brasserie, with its terrace facing Daniel Libeskind’s iconic Kö-Bogen building.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel VILLINO in Lindau
ld.description: A former carpentry workshop in the apple orchards above Lindau, converted by the Fischer family in 1992 and still run by them today, mother Sonja and daughter Alisa between them. The setting is pretty special: fruit trees, an English-Italian garden, and Lake Constance beyond. Chef Toni Neumann's restaurant has held its star for decades, his kitchen finding something unexpected in the space between Japanese technique and southern Italian produce. Rooms range from warm, traditionally furnished doubles to light-filled attic suites with sloped ceilings and terrace views across the orchard.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: ROEWERS Privathotel in Ostseebad Sellin
ld.description: This group of pretty villas has been combined to create a beautifully kept hotel, always on the lookout for ways to improve the service it offers its guests. The rooms are comfortable and elegant, the staff attentive and the 1ha private grounds close to the beaches of the Baltic coast are home to a lovely spa.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Exquisit in Oberstdorf
ld.description: Only the highest quality materials, local wood and homely fabrics have been used to renovate this hotel which now epitomises modern elegance in its comfortable and tasteful design. Guests can also look forward to delicious and sophisticated dishes in the restaurant. Half board included.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Breitenburg in Breitenburg
ld.description: On the vast estate dominated by the 19th-century Breitenburg Castle, alongside the 27-hole Schloss Breitenburg Golf Club, is a very modern luxury hotel by the name of Hotel Breitenburg. Built from the castle’s old stables, with a substantial contemporary addition, it comprises 80 rooms, each one decked out in stylish modern furniture and finished with lumber from the Breitenburger Forest. There’s a capacious and thoroughly equipped spa and wellness center, and the hotel’s restaurant, Johann, serves dishes crafted from painstakingly sourced local and seasonal ingredients, including venison harvested from within the grounds of the Breitenburg estate itself.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Sonnenalp Resort in Ofterschwang
ld.description: No one does mountain resorts quite like Germany, and the expansive Sonnenalp in Ofterschwang is exemplary of the form. Still family-run, it’s slowly grown over the course of a century into what it is today: a four-season escape combining Alpine tranquility, contemporary luxury, and a characteristic focus on wellness. Accommodations range from singles to private lodges and chalets; restaurants include a hearty breakfast, multiple fine-dining options, and much in between. And for leisure there’s the 20,000-square-meter Sonnenalp Wellness World, in addition to facilities for golf, tennis, horse riding and just about every winter sport you’d care to name.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Wald & Schlosshotel Friedrichsruhe in Zweiflingen
ld.description: This luxury country-house hotel boasts rooms ranging from modern to classical castle flair, top-class service, a golf course on the doorstep and grounds ideal for a stroll. The 4,400m2 spa comes with all the trimmings of an indoor and outdoor pool, saunas, a fitness room, a female-only space, and an extensive treatment menu. There are four restaurants to choose from plus a bar and a cigar lounge, but for gastronomes the highlight will be the Two-MICHELIN-Star restaurant Le Cerf.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Maximilian in Oberammergau
ld.description: Sitting in the heart of Oberammergau at the foot of the Ammergau Alps, Maximilian makes a cozy retreat for visitors to Bavaria’s largest nature reserve. Traditional rooms have been designed to cocoon with tactile fabrics and wooden beamed ceilings, and each comes with a view of the natural surroundings. Restaurant Ammergau Maxbräu also doubles up as a brewery where the hotel makes and serves its own craft beer, and in summer guests can also take their drinks outside to the shaded beer garden, which looks across the Ammergau Alps. The spa area is just the tonic after a day out exploring, hiking, and skiing with a Finnish sauna, steam room, whirlpool, hay bath and a selection of beauty and massage treatments.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: HUBERTUS Mountain Refugio Allgäu in Oberallgäu
ld.description: Less than two miles from the Austrian border in Germany’s Allgäuer Mountains is a luxury hotel with a name as unique as its setting: HUBERTUS Mountain Refugio Allgäu, a 66-room ski-to-door lodge designed for mountain comfort. Alpine-style rooms, solid wood furniture, and unpretentious décor define the interiors; outside, it’s all about nature. Guests can exit the hotel and immediately access a cable car station, and the Balderschwang ski area is just beyond the door. Should you want to venture a little farther out, Germany’s longest year-round toboggan run is just a short drive away. Not that you need to go anywhere at all — Slow Food–inspired cuisine is served outside on the terrace, with panoramic views of the mountains to enjoy.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Schlosshotel Burg Schlitz in Hohen Demzin
ld.description: North Germany’s Mecklenburg lakeland is a landscape right out of history, crisscrossed by meandering streams and crowned with castles. Castle Hotel Burg Schlitz is a classic (and Classical) example of the latter, a noble 1806 edifice set on 400 acres of painstakingly landscaped parks and pastures. Just 14 rooms and four suites are available, which speaks to service standards larger hotels can’t hope to match. Each is a uniquely furnished chamber of old-world elegance, down to the oiled floorboards, gilt frames, silken fabrics, and antique candlesticks.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: 1884 Norderney in Norderney
ld.description: The East Frisian island of Norderney is one of those places where you can find an unlikely thing: a German beach. And on the island’s western tip, mere steps from the town center, is 1884 Norderney, a Wilhelminian villa named for the year of its construction. Life may be simple here, but it’s remarkably stylish as well, both in the soothingly minimalist rooms and suites, many of which have views out to sea, and in the spa, with its Finnish sauna and bio-sauna. Not to be overlooked: Müllers auf Norderney, where chef Nelson Müller serves casual yet high-quality fare inspired by home cooking.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hof Galerie in Sylt
ld.description: Combining modern interior design and art, the Hof Galerie offers smart suites, a pretty garden, exhibitions of work by local island artists and a terrace complete with fountain shaded by mature lime trees – perfect for breakfast. In the afternoon, coffee and home-made cakes; until 6pm, light meals in the hotel's bakery opposite.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Wellness & Sport Hotel Jagdhof in Röhrnbach
ld.description: The Wellness & Sporthotel Jagdhof sums up the Bavarian good life in its name alone. Just south of the Bavarian Forest national park, where the German, Czech, and Austrian borders converge, it’s a classic holiday resort with a dizzying array of options to exert oneself and recover afterwards. No judgment for just relaxing, of course — posting up on a lounger with a spritzer and a good book is par for the course around here. But if you’re feeling inclined then there’s all manner of fitness, wellness and beauty facilities to take advantage of — in fact there might be no other wellbeing area quite like this in Germany. There are huge indoor and outdoor pools, a natural bathing lake, tons of fitness classes, saunas and a steam room, a female-only spa space, and beauty treatments that range from traditional massages to the latest cosmetic treatments — and the list goes on. Rooms up the cozy factor with warm earth tones, natural wood, and plush textiles, balanced by floral accents and balconies to invite a little nature in.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Hotel Deimann in Schmallenberg
ld.description: Hotel Deimann has the advantage of being located in Schmallenberg, Germany, a town known for its restorative climate and astounding natural beauty. Even better, this former estate can back that up with thoughtful design and timeless hospitality. From its traditional wood façade to its plentiful gardens to its expansive onsite spa, Deimann makes for the ideal Sauerland getaway. Around here, daily walks pay off: the hotel manages both a golf course café and a forest hut with local pilsner on tap, plus weekly barbecues.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Hotel Romantischer Winkel - RoLigio® & Wellness Resort

ld.name: Hotel Romantischer Winkel - RoLigio® & Wellness Resort in Bad Sachsa
ld.description: Romantischer Winkel is German for “Romantic Corner,” a sensible name indeed for this relaxation-oriented escape in Lower Saxony’s picturesque Harz Mountains, still family-owned and -operated after nearly fifty years. Untouched by urban boutique-hotel aesthetics, it’s as family-friendly as it is romance-oriented, and its devotion to wellness is unyielding — the RoLigio spa aims for a transformation that’s more than skin deep.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Maximilian's in Augsburg
ld.description: Though its history can be traced to the year 1495, this Augsburg institution was completely rebuilt in 1954, and in its current form is as up-to-date as a contemporary luxury hotel can be. Maximilian’s is named for its position on the Maximilianstrasse, and, further back for the emperor of the same name; its style, however modern, is full of historical flourishes. Sartory, the gourmet restaurant, earned its first MICHELIN Star in 2019.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Villa Contessa in Bad Saarow
ld.description: The lakeside resort town of Bad Saarow, on the shores of the Märkisches Meer, is the setting for the lovely Villa Contessa, actually a pair of villas in a unique French Riviera style, accompanied by a fine restaurant and an unusually lavish spa. Classic aesthetics and a remarkable dedication to the white end of the color chart are accompanied by high-end comforts and thoroughly soothing views of the hotel’s natural setting.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Parkhotel Adler in Hinterzarten
ld.description: Black Forest hotels seem to have all the luck — gorgeous views, sporty attractions, period architecture, you name it. Parkhotel Adler is no exception, building on more than half a millennium of hospitality on a vast tract of evergreen-studded woodland with both a duck pond and a lake right around the proverbial corner.A pair of pools and jacuzzis, indoor and out, wrap it all up nicely.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: niXe Boutiquehotel & Spa in Binz
ld.description: Dating from 1903, this picture-perfect villa with modern outbuildings is an annexe of the HOTEL AM MEER & SPA, and a real gem. Guests enjoy smart designer guestrooms (the sea view from some of the rooms is quite spectacular), a good breakfast and pleasant, personalised service.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Diepeschrather Mühle in Bergisch Gladbach
ld.description: On the outskirts of Bergisch Gladbach, close to Cologne, chef Nelson Müller has created a lovely rural refuge. Relais & Châteaux Hotel Diepeschrather Mühle is the classic full-spectrum, chef-driven hospitality experience: a small but luxurious hotel, made up of a mere 25 rooms, suites, and villas, accompanied by a fine restaurant or two. In this case Mr. Mühle has relocated the award-winning gourmet restaurant Schote from Essen to the country, and added the more casual (though scarcely less artful) Müllers in der Mühle. A German luxury hotel, small or otherwise, wouldn’t be complete without a spa and a wellness area — this one with a sauna, hammam, and swimming pool.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: The Wellem in Dusseldorf
ld.description: The century-old courthouse building that now houses The Wellem is nothing if not grand; behind a façade lined with columns you’ll find a vast lobby criscrossed with stone staircases. Hints of contemporary design mark the interior, however, and by the time you’re inside one of the studios and suites, you’re treated to a modern, boutique hotel–inspired experience; colorful, memorable, and full of art. Kitchens or kitchenettes are universal, as are en-suite washers and dryers. The central location places you close to much of the best of Düsseldorf, while the hotel’s own bars and restaurants make a strong case for staying in.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Gut Immenhof in Malente
ld.description: Hotel Gut Immenhof presides, as it has for many years, over Germany’s lush Wagria countryside, a landscape rich with lakes and wildflowers. Its 12 buildings form a renovated country estate, as well known for its equestrian facilities as for its charming rural atmosphere. No two rooms are identical, though fresh color schemes and warm lighting bring an overarching unity to the property. A local store sells farmstand favorites, and kids will love the ponies.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel Oswald Gourmet & Spa in Kaikenried
ld.description: The titular family behind the Hotel Oswald Gourmet & Spa have their roots in butchery and innkeeping, both of which are in ample evidence at this flagship property on the main drag of Kaikenried, Germany. As the name suggests, full-body relaxation is the name of the game — the maximalist spa spans all manner of pools, saunas, and treatment rooms. The hotel is also home to the TWO-MICHELIN-Star restaurant Oswald's Gourmetstube. Cozy rooms come with oceans of natural wood and furnished balconies.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hotel BEI SCHUMANN in Kirschau
ld.description: Hotel Bei Schumann sprouts like an Art Deco bloom from the gentle, meadowed highlands, peacefully at one with its surroundings. The Romanesque dome-and-column spa is a particular draw, especially because guest volume is restricted to keep crowding and noise to a minimum. Rooms speak to the region’s artisan heritage with blonde wood and warming textiles, most featuring captivating views over the undulating landscape. The hotel’s newest wing emphasizes sustainable eco-architecture in a set of junior suites with a suspended pool.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Hüttenhof - Wellnesshotel & Luxus-Bergchalets in Grainet
ld.description: Deep in the Bavarian Forest, the Paster family has invested generations of expertise into Hüttenhof, their wellness-focused spa hotel. A small selection of onsite facilities includes multiple saunas, a full-service spa, an infinity pool, and panoramic views from relaxation spaces throughout the property. Rooms add contemporary verve and eclectic furnishings over a cozy, wood-and-stone foundation. Or spring for a luxury chalet for unparalleled views and privacy (and an individual spa).

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Chiemgauhof Lakeside Retreat in Übersee
ld.description: In contrast with many of the hotels that line the shore of Lake Chiemsee, which are mostly characterized by alpine charm and old-world Bavarian tradition, the cutting-edge Chiemgauhof Lakeside Retreat is a breath of fresh air. Milanese architect Matteo Thun took inspiration from the natural landscape in his designs for the modern luxury hotel, employing native materials like wood and stone, and of course, plenty of glass to make the most of the Chiemgauhof’s position on the water’s edge.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Romantik Hotel Residenz am See in Meersburg
ld.description: The “sea” in question at Romantik Hotel Residenz am See is Lake Constance — as seen from the hotel’s location on the edge of Meersburg, a medieval German town on the lake’s north shore. Accommodations and facilities have been designed to capitalise on that panorama with many of the contemporary rooms looking across the lake, some from their own private balconies. Casala - das Restaurant also comes with a Lake Constance view, and puts its own spin on local cuisine using seasonal ingredients and herbs from the hotel’s own garden. Guests can also try their hand in the kitchen by booking one of the hotel’s cooking classes.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Waldorf Astoria Berlin in Berlin
ld.description: No longer is the Waldorf Astoria name synonymous with Gilded Age New York luxury — though this modern tower, standing tall above Berlin’s City West district, contains more than a few knowing nods to the Art Deco style of the Park Avenue original. Waldorf Astoria Berlin is, at its heart, a thoroughly up-to-date luxury hotel, one that combines contemporary architecture, modern design, historical inspiration and local culture in roughly equal measure.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Das König Ludwig Inspiration SPA in Schwangau
ld.description: Neuschwanstein Castle looms above the village of Schwangau, and the König Ludwig has built something worthy of the address. An adults-only resort run by the Lingenfelder family, it sprawls across 50,000 square meters of Allgäu countryside with privacy and space as its guiding principles. The spa alone covers 7,100 square meters, with treatments tailored individually to each guest. The kitchen sources game from the hotel's own land and works closely with local suppliers throughout the seasons. Unobstructed views across the alpine meadows expand in every direction, and the level of personal attention here reflects decades of family ownership.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Lifestyle Resort Zum Kurfürsten in Bernkastel-Kues
ld.description: On the Moselle above Bernkastel-Kues, Zum Kurfürsten is very much the product of one man's taste. Owner Heiner Buckermann has spent years shaping the place into something he calls retro-chic-stylish: button-back upholstered beds, walnut paneling, pendant chandeliers, and gold accents that feel personal rather than formulaic. The spa is the real reason to come: twelve individually themed saunas, three heated pools, and a natural bathing lake that would justify the trip alone, with a Traditional Chinese Medicine programme adding a dimension few properties in the region can match.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are allowed on request. Charges may apply.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Wellness & Naturresort Reischlhof in Wegscheid
ld.description: Thirty minutes from Passau in the Bavarian Forest, the Reischlhof has been family-run for generations and has built a loyal following on the back of sheer scale and personal attention. The numbers tell part of the story: 5,000 square meters of spa facilities, seven themed saunas, 16 relaxation rooms, a cryotherapy chamber at -85°C, and a 40,000-square-metre forest spa with a natural bathing lake. The kitchen handles regional ingredients with real care. For guests after something beyond standard spa fare, a dedicated longevity program adds a more purposeful dimension to the stay.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

pages.h1: Steigenberger Icon Europäischer Hof Baden Baden

ld.name: Steigenberger Icon Europäischer Hof Baden Baden in Baden-Baden
ld.description: This storied hotel has stood at the center of Baden-Baden since 1840, once a favorite of royals and artists drawn to the town’s thermal waters. Now fully restored and reopened in 2025, returning with polished interiors, rich textures, and a clear respect for its past. Expect high-ceilinged rooms with bespoke details, a rooftop bar overlooking the Black Forest, and a spa designed for real downtime. Right outside: the Kurhaus, the theater, and leafy parkland made for slow strolls. A historic landmark with its feet firmly in the present.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: Botanic Sanctuary Antwerp in Antwerp
ld.description: City-center boutique hotels don’t get much greener than the Botanic Sanctuary Antwerp, set within the walls of the city’s botanical gardens. Here a monastery complex, some of whose buildings date back as far as the 12th century, has been transformed into a 21st-century luxury hotel, alongside a spectacular modern spa. The rooms and suites are delightfully varied and uniformly luxe, the spa is nothing short of sublime, and the hotel’s four restaurants are impressive as well, featuring outposts of the Antwerp-based Hertog Jan and and Fine Fleur (with three Michelin stars between them).
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: Two MICHELIN Keys · An exceptional stay

ld.name: La Butte aux Bois in Lanaken
ld.description: On the edge of Hoge Kempen National Park, near the border of Belgium and the Netherlands, the elegant Domaine La Butte aux Bois occupies a historic estate that dates back to 1924. Rooms and suites are spread out across three buildings: Le Manoir, the grand villa that once served as a nobleman’s residence and also houses the hotel’s dining venues, the more contemporary La Villa, overlooking a small lake, and La Forêt, the newest of the three, with floor-to-ceiling windows facing the surrounding forest. All feature sophisticated interiors with neutral color palettes and refined materials; a few in the main building stand out with creative themes, like the Jewel Suite Missoni, stylistically inspired by the Italian designer, and the Moonlight Suite with its circular sleeping nook and simulated starry sky.
ld.petsAllowed: \n Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Faubourg 21 in Brussels
ld.description: Faubourg 21 aims to combine grand-hotel opulence with boutique-hotel personality on a residential, rather than institutional, scale. It’s set in a 19th-century townhouse across from the Palais Royal and the Royal Quarter’s museums, but it’s hidden behind an elegant but unassuming façade. A previous owner consciously styled it after a French château, and its interiors retain much of their Louis XVI character; to this background Faubourg 21’s current proprietors add a contemporary designer’s eye and a host of modern-luxe fixtures and furnishings.
ld.petsAllowed: Pets are not allowed.

award.awardFor: One MICHELIN Key · A very special stay

ld.name: Château de Vignée in Rochefort
ld.description: Château de Vignée, an 17th-century manor and farmhouse in the Ardennes, is a perfectly lovely place, a red-brick castle whose turrets evoke storybook adventures. Inside, it’s surprisingly contemporary, its rooms and suites presenting a soothingly sedate vision of modern luxury. What elevates it into something extraordinary is the presence of its restaurant, Arden, where chef Marius Bosmans, a veteran of some of Belgium’s finest kitchens, prepares dishes crafted from vegetables grown in the hotel’s own greenhouse.
